# Implementation and validation record

The Windows feature deliverable is complete under ADR002's delivery priority dated
2026-10-31. It includes the functional M1–M3 editor/workspace/translation baseline,
M4 writing modes, extended Markdown and legacy diagrams, visual tables, typography
and local CSS, presentation/image export, optional Pandoc, local command plugins,
explicit folder/WebDAV sync and a verified local installer. Iteration104 below records
the final retained application and acceptance evidence.

Historical cross-platform/physical input/AT and performance qualifications remain
separately tracked. Google Cloud/LibreTranslate are optional provider follow-ups.
Public signing, notarization and publication were not performed; automatic-update
metadata hooks are available, but there is no installed automatic-update client.
See [distribution instructions](../development/distribution.md) and [ADR002](../adr/002-implementation-plan.md).

Launched runtime: Electron 45.0.0, Node 24.22.0, Chromium 156.0.8078.48,
SQLite 3.53.4 (runtime version only; database operations are not implemented).

Artifacts: `apps/desktop/release/Manuslip Setup 0.1.0.exe` and
`apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Manuslip.exe`. Build output is ignored by Git.
Playwright screenshots/traces are in ignored `test/e2e/results/` and regenerated by tests.

CI builds once per OS/architecture, archives the output (tar preserves executable permissions
and symlinks), and reuses it in dedicated E2E jobs with Xvfb on Linux. No installer is rebuilt
for an E2E scenario. Unsigned PR builds require no release secrets and never publish.

Preferences are main-owned electron-store `preferences.json` with `schemaVersion: 1` in
Electron's user-data directory. Development uses `Manuslip Development`; tests create and
remove temporary profiles. Future versions are never passed to electron-store, avoiding
automatic rewrite by defaults. No credentials or document bodies are stored in P0.

The main entry is ES modules to load electron-store without CommonJS interop ambiguity;
the preload is one CommonJS bundle to work inside Electron's sandbox.

## Remaining work

P0's three numbered gates remain unchecked until actual cross-platform installation/launch
results exist; the local implementation and Windows evidence above do not prove those results.

Items 04–06 are implemented and verified locally as described below; their cross-platform
acceptance remains open. Next: M1b semantics/Live Preview, M2 workspace/export, M3 structural
translation, and separately designed M4 features. Their correctness and performance gates
remain unverified.

## M1a — 2026-10-23

The app now provides one mounted CodeMirror source editor with GFM highlighting, locally
loaded fenced-code languages, history, multiple selections, indentation/completion, and
localized find/replace. Zustand stores metadata/status only. New/Open/Save/Save As/Save Copy
use main-owned file sessions and native dialogs; no renderer operation accepts a disk path.

| Gate | Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean dependencies and checks | Fresh `npm ci`; `npm run check` | Passed; same local Electron mirror/checksum policy as P0 |
| Unit/integration tests | `npm test` | 71 passed, one POSIX-mode test skipped on Windows, across 13 files |
| Built application | `npm run test:e2e` | Nine flows: file round trip, cancellation/quit, encoding/newlines, conflicts, interrupted-session recovery, editor UI, future settings, malformed settings, shell security/preferences |
| Packaged application | `npm run build`; `npm run test:packaged` | Nine flows against ASAR-packaged Windows executable; unsigned NSIS installer generated |
| Captured save baseline | Delayed save + newer edits, queued Save As, undo/redo, cancelled save, Save Copy | Acknowledgements advance only the captured baseline; newer equal content clears dirty state without reusing revisions |
| Bytes and limits | Unicode, UTF-8/UTF-16 BOMs, CRLF/CR, legacy encoding round trips, malformed bytes, mixed endings, sparse over-cap input, over-cap edit | Originals preserved; uncertain decoding, unrepresentable characters, and mixed endings require an explicit choice; 50 MiB input and UTF-8 editor limits enforced |
| Atomic failure boundaries | Injected ENOSPC before write/replace; bounded lock retries; outside edits on retry; process exits immediately before/after rename | Original or complete replacement survives; ordinary failures clean temporary files; no unlink-original fallback |
| Metadata/identity | Protected Windows ACL retained exactly; actual case behavior; shared-file records; hard-link refusal; failed Save As watcher cleanup | Passed on local Windows filesystem; POSIX preservation test awaits corresponding runners |
| Autosave/recovery deadlines | Fake-clock continuous edits and a slow save; two-second/ten-second checkpoints; stale clear/checkpoint races; quota | 750 ms idle / five-second dirty scheduling and size-dependent checkpoint cadence verified; storage failure preserves editing and previous snapshot |
| External changes | Parent-directory watches, fingerprint checks, clean reload vs dirty conflict; explicit overwrite confirmation | Dirty buffers retained; self-save events do not overwrite newer edits; cancellation retains content |
| Recovery restart | Abrupt application exit after checkpoint, restart, offer/restore, save to new path | Disk file untouched; recovered content remains dirty until saved/discarded; obsolete snapshot removed after durable save |
| Editor interface | Theme syntax/status contrast, native 200% zoom, English/Chinese labels and search, light/dark/recovery screenshots | Passed for reviewed flows; no screen-reader or physical IME walkthrough yet |

Recovery lives under `userData/recovery`. Files contain a versioned, bounded JSON header and
UTF-8 body, with opaque IDs as filenames. The quota is 100 valid snapshots / 512 MiB, with
64 KiB headers; replacement may temporarily retain both old and new files until commit.
Existing drafts are never silently evicted. Invalid/future snapshots remain untouched.
Restoring creates an untitled session; the original checkpoint survives until a replacement
checkpoint or user-directed save/discard succeeds. A recovery-storage startup error is
visible and does not prevent source editing.

Windows replacement copies and verifies the source ACL using the operating system's static
PowerShell helper, launched without a shell window, profile, or interpolated commands.
POSIX replacement delegates metadata copying to system `cp`; those platform tests still need
actual CI. Hard-linked targets are refused with Save Copy guidance. Existing symlink aliases
resolve to their target before session creation; replacement itself refuses a symlink race.

Filesystem limits: pre-replacement fingerprints reduce conflicts but cannot lock unrelated
applications out of the final check/rename interval. File data is flushed and parent directories
are flushed where supported; Windows directory flush and power-loss durability are not claimed.
A process killed before rename can leave an uncommitted sibling temporary file; it does not
replace the original. Recovery remains subject to its checkpoint interval and storage health.

Still required before the M1a acceptance gate can close: actual macOS/Linux packaged runs and
native shortcuts/metadata behavior, filesystem alias coverage for UNC/junctions and symlinks,
physical IME testing, and broader large-document latency/memory measurements. The plan boxes
remain unchecked until those results exist. At the M1a checkpoint, semantic workers, Live
Preview, tabs/workspaces, assets, exports, and translation were still unimplemented.

## M1b implementation — 2026-10-23

`packages/core` now parses position-bearing whole-document mdast using unified/remark with
GFM, frontmatter and math. Lezer retains its incremental editor-only role. One semantic worker
per window has one running request and one newest pending request, 150 ms idle / 1 s maximum
publication scheduling, an 8 MiB message limit, a separate 16 MiB cache, and a 5 s watchdog.
After three automatic restarts per 60 s, the app retains editable Source and offers Retry.
Generation, revision and configuration checks reject obsolete results. Source materialization
happens in the debounced callback rather than each keystroke.

Documents up to 2 MiB / 50,000 semantic blocks default to Live Preview; larger documents open
directly in Source. Both modes reconfigure the same CodeMirror state/history. Content changes
immediately invalidate old widgets. Inline formatting is scoped to visible ranges, while
layout-changing replacements come directly from a StateField. Selection and composition expose
source. Task checkboxes dispatch normal undoable changes. Tables and highlighted code reveal
source on click; math and mhchem run in a separate lazy, terminable MathJax SVG worker with
local fonts and bounded input, queue, timeout and cache. Unrenderable formulas retain source.

Whole-root mdast-to-HAST rendering resolves references before extracting widget fragments.
Every HTML/SVG DOM sink uses DOMPurify. HTML defaults to escaped text; explicit raw-HTML
permission still sanitizes it. HTTPS links use a validated native browser route. Raster data
images and opaque app-image assets are supported; SVG data URLs and unsafe URL protocols are
rejected. Remote images default off and require a native confirmation per open document.
The main proxy validates public DNS/IPs and pins connections, rechecks redirects, excludes
browser credentials/cookies, and enforces raster MIME, byte, time, concurrency and memory
limits. Revocation/close abort requests and remove assets; late results cannot restore them.
The fixed CSP permits only the app image scheme in addition to its original image sources;
document permission never changes it or enables renderer network connections.

| Gate | Local evidence | Result / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean dependency install | Fresh `npm ci`, exact lockfile | Passed on Windows with existing Electron mirror/checksum policy |
| Static checks | `npm run check` | Lint, format, process boundaries and strict types passed |
| Unit/integration tests | `npm test` | 752 passed, one POSIX-only test skipped, across 21 files |
| CommonMark | All 652 official 0.31.2 examples, normalized HTML before application security restrictions | Passed; pinned corpus and upstream license included as test-only data |
| Semantic correctness | GFM/frontmatter/math, full-root references, position offsets, duplicate range identity, split/merge/reset | Passed for included fixtures |
| Scheduling/failure | Fake-worker latest-pending, generation/config races, debounce/max delay, watchdog/restart cap; real worker crash E2E | Passed; real Retry restores preview after four failed worker instances |
| Editing continuity | Live/Source switching, selection, undo, edits after cached preview restoration, task toggles | Passed in Electron E2E |
| HTML/image admission | Malicious HTML, unsafe URL tests; actual browser DOM checks and native permission allow/cancel/revoke | Scripts/event handlers/iframes removed; no ambient image requests; private destinations denied |
| Proxy isolation | Mixed public/private DNS, pinned lookup, redirect to loopback, DNS cancellation, permission and late-result races | Passed with injected network transport; no live remote image service used for verification |
| Built/packaged Windows | Full 14-flow suite, including 1 MiB performance corpus and worker failure/size fallback | Passed against built app and ASAR-packaged executable; installer rebuilt |

The latest packaged 1 MiB prose run recorded p95 input-to-next-animation-frame 3.2 ms, semantic request
preparation 3.0 ms, and snapshot apply 3.3 ms; the last snapshot settled in about 363 ms including
debounce. These are local observations, not a complete performance gate. Input-to-frame is a
paint proxy, not a compositor presentation timestamp. Local `performance.measure` entries
record request, validation, worker parse/describe/render/serialization, transport, apply and
freshness without document text or network telemetry. The Playwright JSON attachment retains
the measurements for each run.

Still open for M1b acceptance: physical Chinese/Japanese IME and screen-reader walkthroughs;
actual macOS/Linux packaged results; retained-memory stress and repeated mode changes; richer
table/math/nested-container performance corpora; scroll-anchor and multiple-selection stress;
and sustained apply/yield budgets beyond the measured prose fixture. Existing Windows results
do not close those gates. At this checkpoint, M2 tabs/workspaces/navigation/local assets/exports
and M3 translation and bilingual layouts were not yet implemented.

## M2 document tabs — 2026-10-23

New/Open and recovery restoration now add documents to a tab collection. Only the active
CodeMirror view is mounted; inactive documents retain their editable state, selection, undo
history and mapped scroll anchor. Their autosave, recovery checkpoints and file-change
subscriptions continue. Unmount releases semantic snapshots, occurrence metadata, Live widget
decorations and mounted rendering jobs; reactivation requests current semantics through the
same bounded window worker. Counts/outline are repopulated when current semantics settle.

Main reuses an existing file session when native Open resolves to the same file in that window.
The tab collection activates it without applying the fresh disk snapshot to its buffer.
Save As refuses a destination already open in another tab. The 32-tab limit is enforced in
main, including recovery restoration; a rejected open releases its unused file record/watcher.
This limit does not establish an aggregate editable-state or undo-history memory bound.

Ctrl/Cmd+W closes the current document; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+W closes the window. A window close
locks all documents and obtains every save/discard decision before disposing any document.
Cancellation retains even earlier drafts marked Discard, unlocks all tabs and resumes autosave.
One window-close request may wait behind a file dialog; duplicate close requests coalesce.
Tabs support arrows/Home/End, a labeled close action, visible dirty marks and localized names.

| Verification | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Static checks and unit/integration suite | `npm run check`; 765 passed, 1 platform-specific skip across 23 test files |
| File/session lifecycle | Same-owner reopen, cross-owner isolation, tab-cap cleanup and Save As collision checks passed |
| Tab lifecycle | Separate dirty drafts, selection and undo restoration, queued/coalesced window close, cancellation without partial disposal, recovery errors and background autosave/reload passed |
| Derived-state lifetime | Suspension releases snapshot/Live model; inactive edits issue no parse; reactivation parses current source |
| Windows built and packaged UI | Full 17-flow suite includes long filenames, both themes, Chinese, keyboard focus/activation/close, 320px reflow and native 200% zoom |

The scroll test exposed two lifecycle issues: view cleanup must capture its anchor before React
removes the DOM, and changing CodeMirror's locale phrases resets its view. Layout-effect cleanup
and an explicit scroll restoration after locale configuration cover both. Full draft bodies,
selection and undo remain in CodeMirror rather than being copied into the tab metadata store.

At this checkpoint, folder tree/recents/session restoration, OS file association/drop, workspace
search, local asset management, isolated diagrams, exports and translation remained pending.
Named-tab session persistence was not yet implemented. Physical IME, screen readers, forced
colors, retained-memory stress and macOS/Linux results remained unverified.

## M2 folder workspaces and session restoration — 2026-10-23

Native Open folder now grants a canonical root to the current window. The sidebar lazily
lists Markdown/text files and directories, excludes `.git`, `node_modules` and links/junctions,
and supports keyboard disclosure, paging and explicit Refresh. Changing folders or refreshing
the catalog preserves open editors and drafts. Opening an already-owned file activates its tab
without replacing its buffer. Save As updates session metadata to the new path.

Main owns paths, root identity and opaque node/recent/restore IDs. Each access rechecks root
identity, containment and directory components; workspace file reads, watcher reloads and
saves retain their grant checks. A replaced directory junction is denied rather than followed.
Refresh revokes old catalog IDs. Listings allow one running request and eight queued, 200 nodes
per page, at most 5,000 entries examined per directory, 10,000 registered nodes, 16 MiB accounted
catalog storage and depth 32. Limits and skipped links are explicit in the UI. These path and
identity checks do not create an OS-level filesystem sandbox or eliminate filesystem check/use
races. Native file selection and Save As remain explicit user grants.

Private versioned session metadata stores the current root, ten recent folders, up to 32 named
file paths in tab order and the active named tab. It contains no document bodies. Renderer
updates debounce for 250 ms and coalesce; main coalesces atomic writes separately. Window close
flushes metadata while file IDs remain owned, after all save/discard decisions. Startup restores
named tabs before persisting a new collection, then offers interrupted draft recovery separately.
Missing roots/files remain visible; unavailable tabs stay in the saved session until reopened
or explicitly removed. Persistence failure offers Retry without blocking source editing.
Corrupt metadata is backed up; future schemas are backed up and kept read-only.

## M2 native file opening and file drops — 2026-10-23

Cold launch paths are queued before application readiness. Later launches use Electron's
single-instance lock for the same profile and forward file arguments to the existing window;
macOS `open-file` is registered before readiness. The renderer pulls queued opaque request IDs
after named-session restoration and recovery-list loading. Opening reuses the existing file
lifecycle and activates an already-owned tab without replacing its dirty buffer. File reads
serialize with editor commands; a cancelled close resumes waiting requests.

Preload intercepts file drops before editor text-drop handlers/navigation, requires a trusted
event and obtains disk paths with `webUtils.getPathForFile`. Synthetic renderer drops and
JavaScript-created files cannot grant access. Only the private preload route submits dropped
paths; the public renderer bridge lists, opens and dismisses main-owned IDs. Native arguments
ignore switches, network URLs and unsupported extensions. Markdown (`md`, `markdown`, `mdown`)
and text (`txt`) paths are accepted; folders use the existing native Open folder action.

The incoming queue holds at most 32 paths, one running read and no document bodies. Paths are
bounded to 32,768 characters. A launch/drop burst over 32 files is rejected visibly; duplicate
queued paths coalesce. Failed opens remain visible with Retry/Dismiss. There is no automatic
retry loop. Explicit window close dismisses that window's remaining external-open requests;
already-open dirty tabs retain the existing save/discard/cancel protection. Late frame/window
results are rejected and their file ownership is revoked.

The NSIS installer compiles a custom Open with registration for `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mdown`
using `Manuslip.Markdown`, application `SupportedTypes` and quoted executable/filename arguments.
Its install/uninstall macros touch only app-owned registration and extension OpenWithProgids;
they do not write extension defaults or UserChoice. macOS advertises Editor/Alternate document
types; Linux advertises `text/markdown` and uses `%F` to receive file paths.

| Editing/lifecycle | Busy-command coalescing, dirty-draft preservation, explicit failure retry/dismissal and resume after cancelling close passed |
| Windows built app | All 22 Electron flows passed; cold startup alongside saved tabs, a real second executable launch, Chromium native file-drop events, synthetic-drop denial and missing-file controls included |
| Interface | Both-theme text contrast at least 4.5:1, keyboard focus/Retry/Dismiss, long paths, Chinese, 320px and native 200% zoom passed; screenshots inspected |
| Windows installer | NSIS installer and uninstaller macros compiled successfully |
| Windows packaged app | Full 22-flow suite passed against the ASAR-packaged executable, including a second executable launch with a filename containing spaces |

The packaged 1 MiB prose run recorded p95 input-to-next-frame 2.9 ms, request preparation
3.0 ms and snapshot apply 2.7 ms; last-result freshness was about 381 ms including debounce.
The same local-measurement limitations and broader open performance gates still apply.

The narrow failure-notice flow exposed editor status text overlapping the footer when vertical
space was exhausted. Editor chrome no longer shrinks and the writing region scrolls when its
minimum contents exceed available height; the geometry regression and existing scroll tests pass.

Still unverified: installation/uninstallation and shell Open with registration on a clean Windows
machine; physical OS drag-and-drop and macOS Finder/Dock events; Linux desktop integration;
assistive technology and forced colors. Emitting `open-file` in Electron tests checks our handler,
not macOS delivery. Chromium drag events check the actual preload/file route, not a physical
Explorer gesture. These limits keep the cross-platform M2 gate open.

isolated diagrams, exports and translation remained pending.

## M2 navigation and offline spelling — 2026-10-23

Implemented whole-document outline/heading jumps, word and character counts, fuzzy path lookup,
and cancellable literal full-text search over saved workspace files. View → Find file
(`Ctrl/Cmd+P`) and Search workspace (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F`) expand the search and focus its input,
including after folder admission or closing Preferences. Native accelerator registration and
menu callback execution are tested; these are not physical OS shortcut-delivery tests.

Search uses pinned `@vscode/ripgrep` 1.18.0 and fuzzysort 4.0.2. The packaged runtime resolves
its own platform/architecture executable, checks the real file/size/executable permission,
and uses `shell: false`, fixed-string arguments and no user ripgrep configuration. It honors
workspace ignore files outside Git repositories, disables parent/global ignore rules, and
excludes links, hidden paths, .git, node_modules and unsupported file extensions. Positive
include globs originally bypassed ignore rules; real-binary tests caught this and the filter
now uses file types plus explicit exclusions. UTF-8 and BOM-marked UTF-16 are supported;
undecodable match lines or unusable locations are skipped visibly. CR-only/changed lines
can be opened, but a location jump is refused if the editor's current line differs.

There is one running process and one replaceable pending job, with a 15 s deadline, two
threads, 20 MiB raw-output/retained-result accounting caps and at most 500 matches. Records
are capped at 2 MiB, match lines at 65,536 UTF-16 units, and filename enumeration at 10,000
candidates or 8 MiB accounting. Limits stop work and produce a truncation notice. IPC batches
and initial result rendering contain at most 50 matches; Show more adds 50. A new query or
folder/Refresh revokes old IDs. Stop kills the process while keeping already-delivered results
openable. Result opening repeats file-grant checks; byte offsets are converted to UTF-16 and
the exact saved line is compared before moving the selection in a dirty tab.

Outline and counts share the active document's existing semantic worker in Source and Live
modes. Jumps use only a current semantic revision and never replace source/history. The UI
initially mounts 200 headings, with another 200 per explicit Show more. Inactive tabs release
derived state and perform no parsing. Existing 2 MiB semantic admission/fallback applies.
Words use Intl word segmentation over prose text nodes, including CJK; characters count
source Unicode code points. Stale counts are hidden rather than shown as current.

Spelling is an optional version-1 preference; older settings remain valid with spelling off.
Windows/Linux use the exact en-US-10-2 dictionary from Electron 45.0.0's release, with its size
and SHA-256 verified before atomic placement in the private cache. The CDN URL is replaced
by the packaged local directory. macOS uses native system languages. Missing/damaged bundled
data disables spelling with reinstall guidance while leaving editing and other preferences
available. Original wordlist notices, provenance and checksums ship in the vendor directory.
The native editing menu offers at most five suggestions; actual corrections participate in
CodeMirror undo. UI controls retain the pending choice during writes, then commit or roll back;
a forced preference-write failure and successful retry are tested.

## M2 clipboard and local assets — 2026-10-23

HTML paste now uses Turndown 7.2.4 and GFM 1.0.2 in a terminable Node worker. It
converts headings, emphasis, lists, tasks, tables and code; table pipes are escaped and
highlighted code fences grow to enclose embedded backticks. Active HTML, unsafe URLs,
and temporary preview capabilities are excluded. Ctrl/⌘ Shift V and code-context paste
retain plain text. A 1 MiB UTF-8 input limit, 4 MiB output limit, one active job, 5-second
deadline and worker heap limits bound conversion. Workers terminate on completion,
failure, document close and window loss.

Image paste captures the native PNG before Save As, then exclusively creates a unique
assets/pasted-UUID.png beside the saved document and inserts a relative Markdown link.
Cancelled Save As preserves the source and releases the capture. Async insertion ranges
map through unrelated edits; changes within a selected replacement cancel the paste
rather than overwrite those edits. Each completed paste is one undo step. Imports remain
on disk after undo, link deletion and document close.

Local PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP reads use captured workspace/parent grants and opaque protocol
capabilities. Containment, directory identities, intermediate links/junctions, file
identity and bounded file reads are rechecked. Dimensions are checked before browser
admission; the 64 MiB cache counts compressed bytes plus an RGBA-size estimate, with
256 entries, four active reads and 32 pending jobs. A clipboard capture is bounded to
20 MiB, 16 million pixels, 8192 pixels per side, one per window and 60 seconds. Local SVG,
absolute/drive/UNC/ADS paths and grant escapes are rejected. Windows case matching
preserves canonical authorization. Save As refreshes image widgets in the new directory;
original files remain. Missing/blocked images explain the failure and offer retry.

| Gate | Evidence / result |
| --- | --- |
| Static checks | Biome lint/format, import boundaries and strict TypeScript passed |

## M2 isolated Mermaid diagrams — 2026-10-23

Mermaid 12.2.0 now loads on first use in a hidden, sandboxed Electron renderer with DOM
access, a separate non-persistent session/custom origin and a different OS process from
the editor. Its standalone preload exposes only host ready/job/result messages. Main-frame
identity and URL checks protect those messages; the normal editor bridge is unavailable.
Network/file fetches, popups, navigation, permissions, frames and workers are denied.
Only built entry/script/style/font assets are served. Document configuration directives and
YAML frontmatter are rejected; strict security, SVG labels and dagre/classic remain fixed.

Main owns one running job and four pending jobs per window, prioritizes visible consumers,
replaces obsolete occurrences, enforces a 3-second deadline including host startup, and
allows three automatic restarts within 60 seconds before manual Retry. Hung obsolete jobs
still count against that budget; deliberate document/window revocation does not. Renderer
admission allows 200 mounted consumers and five IPC jobs. The main SVG cache is an 8 MiB
LRU; displayed markup participates in the existing 16 MiB widget budget. Source is capped
at 64 KiB UTF-8, SVG at 2 MiB, semantic/rendered nodes at 2,000, SVG elements at 20,000 and
Mermaid edges at 4,000. Known database collections are checked before layout, with a
rendered-node check afterwards and a process watchdog around the entire operation.

Generated CSS is flattened into explicit presentation attributes before style/classes are
removed. Active HTML, links, images, animation and style blocks are excluded, and SVG is
sanitized again at editor admission. Each mounted SVG receives distinct IDs; references
must resolve inside that copy. The SVG URI policy now explicitly preserves inert geometry
and presentation attributes, fixing discarded transforms/paths in both diagrams and math.
Errors retain the original source, provide localized guidance and keep Retry keyboard
reachable. Retrying preserves focus; theme changes cancel obsolete output and rerender.
Source text and undo history remain unchanged by rendering.

| Diagram fidelity | Packaged cold first render and flowchart, sequence, class, state, entity, pie and Gantt fixtures, including Unicode; SVG geometry and separated labels asserted |
| Host isolation | Packaged different PID/session, sandbox/context isolation, no Node/editor bridge, hidden host, denied popup and HTTPS/file/non-asset fetches |
| Failure recovery | Actual infinite loop in the isolated process; editor input and native save succeed, another sandboxed window responds, main kills the old PID, source/error remain, Retry succeeds in a fresh host |

## M3 offline structural translation harness — 2026-10-24

ADR 002 item 15 is implemented in `packages/translate`. Paragraph, heading and table-cell
units retain UTF-16 ranges, caller-supplied occurrence identities, AST paths and private
reconstruction bindings. Lists, block quotes and footnote definitions contribute their prose
units while retaining outer structure. Paired canonical tokens preserve emphasis, deletion
and human-readable Markdown link/reference labels. Atomic tokens preserve inline code/math,
images, raw HTML fragments/bodies, hard breaks, automatic links, URI-looking literal text,
footnote references and literal token delimiters. Whole code, math, diagrams, frontmatter,
HTML and definitions stay untouched. Image alt text currently stays in the protected image.

Provider jobs contain canonical payload/key only. SHA-256 identity includes extraction and
reconstruction schemas, all payload text/token structure, normalized provider routing/model/
profile/options, source and target languages, glossary, formality and prompt version. Secrets
are excluded from descriptor fields. Endpoint normalization rejects user information,
fragments, known credential query/option names and remote HTTP; path, trailing slash and
ordered non-secret query routing remain meaningful. Future adapters must restrict their own
documented options and implement transport/credential protections separately.

Validation requires every expected token exactly once, its original parent and balanced pair;
siblings may reorder. Reconstruction uses text nodes, never provider Markdown/HTML parsing.
Each occurrence restores its own protected nodes. Missing, invalid or oversized results retain
the original unit and report separate statuses; the source/root remain unchanged. Whole-plan
overflow rejects without truncation, and both unit and aggregate reconstructed output are bounded.

## M3 provider transport, credentials and cache — 2026-10-24

ADR 002 item 16 is implemented. Preferences lazily loads a distinct main-owned translation
configuration for OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions or Ollama. The full endpoint, model,
source/target language tags, glossary, prompt-based formality, temperature and output budget
participate in identity. Opening settings creates no provider request or key-store access.
The translated document consumer, Refresh/Retry Failed and bilingual/export integration
remain items 17–19; this checkpoint does not claim a translated reading UI.

Electron 45's actual Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.53.4 passed a CREATE/INSERT/SELECT Unicode
transaction before the adapter was chosen. Cache migration/read/write/eviction runs in one
lazy worker, not the main event loop. The versioned database stores validated canonical
payload/output only; exact payload equality and placeholder validation are repeated on hits.
Two main-owned jobs deduplicate subscriptions, retain their distinct occurrence/context,
and cancel transport only after the last subscriber cancels. Main recomputes every unit key.
Settings changes, owner/document close and cache generation barriers reject obsolete work.
Clear invalidates every owner before serialized derived-cache deletion; late writes cannot
restore cleared entries. Corruption/future schemas/quota/busy/worker failures are explicit,
and successful network output remains usable when persistence fails.

Credentials have a separate write-only IPC method. The uncontrolled password input clears
synchronously, never enters React/Zustand, and receives only none/session/stored status.
Session keys remain in main memory. Optional persistent keys use asynchronous safeStorage
with a 5 s bound, reject Linux basic_text and locked/unavailable key stores, and bind to the
adapter/full endpoint/profile. Future or oversized credential files are preserved. Settings
and encrypted metadata use private atomic JSON files; no credential enters cache identity.

| Focused services | 43 tests: local native transport, OpenAI/Ollama contracts, malformed/truncated/tool/refusal output, redirect origin/POST limits, response caps, 429/backoff/auth/cancel, key-store lock/timeout/rotation, future/oversized credentials, SQLite migration/restart/corruption/future/lock/actual quota failure/LRU, bounded worker queues/watchdog and shared-request cancellation/clear barriers |

| Real OS-protected key | Windows asynchronous safeStorage stores ciphertext only; restart decrypts on explicit translation; status reads never decrypt; platform-unavailable case uses a session key instead |
| Race isolation | Actual held local HTTP responses cancelled or cleared through the bridge; late replies cannot populate cache; source editing still works |
| Settings interface | Keyboard Enter/Escape/focus return, invalid endpoint/glossary, advanced settings persistence, immediate key-input clearing, injected unavailable key store, session alternative, cache confirmation, both themes, Chinese 320px and 200% native zoom; interface review recorded separately |

Limits are defined in ADR 002 and `shared/translation-contracts.ts`: two running jobs,
32 waiting jobs, 128 subscriptions, 256 KiB request/2 MiB response, 60 s total job deadline,
two transient retries and three same-origin POST redirects. The SQLite worker has a 128 MiB

is 96 MiB/20,000 rows in 128-row batches. Database/journal/quarantine accounting stays within

bounds, not proof of the wider performance targets. Source/cache contents remain local
unencrypted user data, except for OS-encrypted optional keys.

## M3 — DeepL provider — 2026-10-24

DeepL now shares the translation scheduler/cache/reconstruction path with OpenAI-compatible
and Ollama providers. It uses native authentication and synthetic XML v2 tags over canonical
prose/token IDs; protected source bindings never enter provider requests. Dynamic stable-language
metadata supplies XML-capable choices, target formality and source/target glossary support.
Existing DeepL glossary IDs are accepted; remote glossary creation is outside this adapter.
Chat model, temperature, output-token and inline glossary controls are absent for DeepL.

Opening preferences or reading remains offline. Load supported languages explicitly contacts
the configured server without document text; cache-miss Translate also discovers support when
needed. The optional full metadata URL must share the translation endpoint's origin. Metadata
has a 256 KiB/512-language cap, ten-second network deadline including retries and one explicit
discovery alongside two unit jobs. One connection's metadata stays in memory for 15 minutes.
Credential/configuration/cache/window changes abort discovery and reject late completion.
Provider JSON is capped at 128 KiB; existing output, queue, redirect and overall unit limits apply.
Missing credentials fail before HTTP; rejected credentials and exhausted quota have distinct
messages. HTTP 456 is never retried. Only user-selected Retry failed issues another attempt.

Translation configuration schema 2 reads schema 1 without rewriting on load, and writes schema
2 on deliberate save. Older versions preserve this new format as future data. Session/OS key
storage and SQLite cache retain their existing behavior; no runtime dependency was added.

## Cooperative semantic application — 2026-10-24

Dense documents no longer reconcile every occurrence and rebuild all widget identities in
one uninterrupted renderer task. Preparation uses a source-ordered range builder and yields
after approximately 1 ms of work, checking progress every 64 descriptors. The native
`scheduler.yield()` continuation allows pending browser input to run; a timer fallback is
available. [Chromium scheduling reference](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/use-scheduler-yield).
The 1 ms scheduling target is not a guarantee for arbitrary individual operations; the
acceptance test independently measures the maximum completed slice against 4 ms.

A new index and widget model remain private until preparation completes. Commit checks
the tracker version; continuation checks the current document body, revision, consumer and
lifetime. Edits, suspend, reset, disposal, locale/render requests and consumer detachment
cancel pending preparation and release its generator/callbacks. Partially prepared models
never become current, update counts or satisfy an export/translation capture. Successful
mode/asset changes reuse the complete prepared widget model. Plain prose skips the unused
widget identity map. Range reuse still verifies exact source text, including hash collisions,
and ambiguity assigns fresh IDs rather than attaching to another duplicate.

The race tests also exposed redundant Retry work: retrying an existing consumer could start
its previous intent just before the current request replaced it. Retry now obtains a new
consumer before clearing the pause and publishing current source/options. Captures requested
during valid apply preparation wait for that preparation instead of restarting it.

## Whole-root transport and dense freshness — 2026-10-24

Semantic results now transfer one owned UTF-8 JSON buffer containing the complete document
and render projection. This avoids structured cloning every AST object and avoids serializing
the decoded root again merely to check message size. Sequence, generation, document and
revision checks precede decoding; actual buffer size, a bounded metadata envelope, fatal UTF-8,
JSON shape and source ranges are checked. The 8 MiB message cap, doubled snapshot accounting,
32 MiB retained-snapshot ledger and 16 MiB worker-cache limit remain. A 1,024-byte envelope
reserve is charged. Cache entries own a separate buffer so transferring a result cannot detach
the cached bytes; entries too large for the cache are never copied into it. The returned
validated snapshot does not retain the encoded payload.

Parsing still consumes the whole source and produces every root node, position, reference,
descriptor and render block. A conservative absence check skips GFM tokenizers only when no
GFM construct is possible; math/frontmatter remain active and ordinary list-item properties
match the complete grammar. Any pipe, tilde, at sign, colon, bracket, ampersand, backslash or
case-insensitive `www.` selects full GFM. Dependency upgrades must rerun the independent
full-grammar oracle. No fragments, delta transport, parser pool, root truncation or higher
resource limit was introduced.

Added `test/benchmark/boundary.spec.ts` to the packaged performance suite. The fixture is exactly
**52,428,800 UTF-8 bytes**, with CJK and supplementary characters on wrapped lines and an
ASCII tail. The actual editor rejects both keyboard growth at the cap and a DOM plain-text

on macOS); its first attempt used the macOS shortcut on Windows and correctly failed the

## Cancellable large plain-text paste — 2026-10-24

Plain-text paste of at least 262,144 UTF-16 units now prepares an immutable CodeMirror text
value in cooperative tasks, then inserts once. Each normalization chunk is at most 65,536
units and preserves a CRLF pair or surrogate pair at a chunk boundary. Normalized UTF-8
bytes are bounded at 50 MiB before completion; the existing final editor-byte transaction
filter also covers current text and multiple selections. No partially prepared text becomes
editable source, dirty state, save content, semantic input or undo history.

The pending status now has a native Cancel paste button in English/Chinese. Escape, tab
suspension, composition start, locking and disposal invalidate insertion and release staged
work. Original selections map through unrelated edits; edits touching a selected replacement
reject it with the existing paste-again message. An explicitly cancelled job does not report
failure or clear the status of a newer job. Previously issued image/conversion bridge calls
may finish, but an invalidated job cannot insert their result. Existing image retention rules
remain. A successful paste is one isolated undo step. The final atomic editor transaction is
not preemptible; this is cancellation during preparation, not interruption midway through
changing the document.

## Cancellable replace all — 2026-10-24

The native search panel now prepares Replace all in one disposable browser worker, then
validates and cooperatively builds a complete ChangeSet before one isolated editor transaction.
The public CodeMirror cursor retains native literal, case, whole-word, Unicode precision,
regex, capture and zero-width semantics. An independent public native replaceAll command
serves as the whole-text and selection oracle. Adjacent matches coalesce without omission;
disjoint records, actual encoded result bytes, source/result UTF-8 size and whole-job elapsed
time have explicit limits in ADR 002. No limit was raised to pass these checks.

Cancel replacement and Escape discard pending work. Editing, changing the query, tab
suspension, composition, locking or disposal invalidate the captured revision; selection-only
changes remain valid. Old responses cannot install. Source, dirty state, saving, semantics
and undo history never receive a partial replacement. Source collection and balanced
ChangeSet preparation yield; worker matching cannot block source editing. The final atomic
transaction and bounded result decoding are not preemptible.

observations on this runtime, not a portable hard shutdown guarantee. Rapid repeated

## Lossless semantic packing experiment — 2026-10-24

The nested performance failure now has an executable lossless representation experiment and
a separate design in [ADR 003](../adr/003-semantic-snapshot-packing.md). The current application
continues using whole-root JSON and explicit Source fallback; no runtime export, protocol,
limit, dependency or installer asset changed at this checkpoint.

The pure experimental codec shares equal value records and keeps exact position coordinates
in a typed table behind enumerable immutable accessors. Full mdast data, source ranges,
references, counts, descriptors and projection are retained. Strict version, bytes, numeric
budgets, canonical varints, UTF-8, schema keys, references, complete consumption and separate
staging/retained ledgers reject malformed or oversized values. Generic value decoding still
requires application identity and semantic-schema/source validation before any runtime use.
No failed decode returns a partial result. Serialization, native cloning and repacking retain
semantic values; a clone may be changed without mutating the captured graph.

## Owned packed arena and bounded subtree access — 2026-10-24

The experimental representation now supports a persistent owned arena with direct indexed
field/array/position reads and independently bounded selected-subtree extraction. It keeps
complete semantics available without retaining a second expanded root in the worker cache.
The expanded decoder uses a typed position-reference vector instead of per-position handles.
Large strings validate in small UTF-8 chunks with JSON escape state across boundaries, remain
uncached, and expose explicit output/workspace costs before selected extraction. Full string
decoding also charges its temporary JSON spelling. ADR 003 records the format, ownership,
weights, measured scope and remaining activation gates.

Successful arena admission transfers ownership and detaches both the incoming buffer and
old typed views. Rejected data or limits preserve the input buffer. Every record, including
unreachable ones, is validated before publication. Private bytes/indexes/metadata are not
exposed. Selected extraction is iterative, preserves shared DAG values without exponential
expansion, returns immutable exact positions and exposes no partial result on failure. It
does not parse changed source or resolve new document-wide dependencies.

`test/artifacts/logs/.arena-check-final.log`: formatting/lint, process boundaries and strict TypeScript
pass. `test/artifacts/logs/.arena-units-final.log`: **3,806 passed**, one POSIX-only Windows skip, 78 files.
The packed representation has **1,386 focused cases**: both expanded and indexed access cover
all 652 CommonMark roots, plus extension data, Unicode/lone surrogates, negative zero,
ownership, reflection resistance, exact limits, invalid IDs/kinds, shared/deep graphs,
selected-subtree isolation and failed admission. String tests cross UTF-8/escape/Unicode
chunk boundaries and reject malformed UTF-8, controls, bad escapes, truncated values and
valid non-string JSON. An initial test incorrectly expected `JSON.parse` to reject `null`;
the corrected independent assertion distinguishes valid JSON from the required string type.

## Packed text spans and repeated updates — 2026-10-24

`packing-text.ts` adds immutable UTF-16 text splices over owned string spans, integrated
with ordered revision operations. Unchanged spans stay in their original arena. Array,
object and text aliases/captured values remain exact. Metadata admission precedes span
construction; invalid kinds/ranges/budgets publish nothing. This avoids whole-HTML storage
replacement, while keeping the complete resulting HTML available as an admitted caller-owned
value. Old arena/overlay reservations still accumulate and need session compaction/resync.

`packing-string.ts` now shares JSON lexical state between validation and bounded chunk
materialization. Fatal streaming UTF-8, escaped units, supplementary carry and lone UTF-16
surrogates remain exact. Chunk output is at most 4,098 UTF-16 units. Direct untrusted reader
iteration can yield a prefix before a malformed suffix rejects; arena cursors expose only
already validated immutable bytes. Tests compare **all 65,536 UTF-16 code units**, chunk
boundaries and malformed inputs against native JSON behavior. The earlier complete codec,
CommonMark and extension suites remain passing.

Text materialization resumes a cursor for each distinct owned string across unchanged spans,
without decoding unrelated scalars or caching long results. Backwards ranges reset that
cursor. `readScalar` admits output and temporary staging before streaming. Staging reserves
join/chunk storage, cursor state and boundary chunks separately from returned UTF-16 output.
Tests verify rejection before reading, exact admission, 150 deterministic Unicode edits
against native JS strings, shared aliases, captured cursors and cuts inside surrogate pairs.

## Whole-document dependency indexing — 2026-10-24

The experimental `packages/core/src/semantic-dependencies.ts` reads a verified whole parser
root through scoped packed readers. It indexes top-level ranges, definition/reference
ranges, first-definition resolution and footnote body/used-footer call order. Duplicate and
unused definition bodies do not affect rendered numbering; cycles and repeated calls retain
the installed renderer's behavior. The immutable result owns its validated exact source and
identity, independently of the capture. It does not retain arenas, readers or the session.
This is a separately admitted caller output, not yet a production cache or a fragment parser.

Testing uncovered valid overlapping upstream ranges in CommonMark example 215: a setext
heading starts at the preceding definition's offset. The index preserves the exact ranges
and marks `disjointBlocks: false` for future fallback. It never repairs those source positions
or treats ambiguous boundaries as permission to reuse a fragment. Literal unresolved bracket
syntax is flagged even when the whole parser emits no reference node.

## Packed suffix position transforms — 2026-10-24

The experimental packed revision protocol now implements the previous checkpoint's suffix
instruction as an ordered `offset` operation. It shifts position-tag offsets only, preserving
all lines/columns and ordinary scalar/object properties. Flat array segments carry the delta;
views compute transformed positions without expanding or re-encoding unchanged descendants.
Repeated shifts combine instead of building a recursive wrapper chain. Newly replaced values
retain absolute positions while old siblings preserve their existing transforms.

Preparation walks every selected suffix position to reject unsigned 32-bit underflow/overflow
before publication. Validation is iterative, with 256-frame and 800,000-visit limits and
admitted scratch. A failed late operation rejects the whole candidate and preserves accepted
data. This first implementation still pays a full suffix-validation cost; it does not claim
constant-time validation or satisfy a renderer apply-slice budget.

and reversed shifts, replacements, splices, text edits, malformed offsets/ranges, exact

length-changing edits in different blocks each compare with an independent complete fresh
root; earlier captures compare again after the sequence. Positive fragment tests now also
prepare, inspect and commit real packed roots and compare the old capture, alongside their

## Cooperative packed receipt and queued ownership — 2026-10-24

`PackedReceiver.receiveSteps` admits incoming bytes, normalized wire metadata and continuation
control slots before exposing a scheduler handle. It transfers admitted binary ownership
immediately, detaching the caller's wrapper, and retains the existing source/base-token
checks. Later caller envelope mutations cannot change the queued result. Failed envelope/base
checks or failed admission leave the caller's buffer untouched. No uncharged payload can sit
inside an unstarted receiver generator.

The handle yields before preparation and validation, then advances a synchronous validator
iterator. Only complete successful validation and cleanup commit the snapshot and emit its
accepted acknowledgement. Ordinary promises, async iterators, malformed steps and non-void
returns fail without publication. The synchronous `receive` API remains explicit. Cancellation,
newer requests, eviction, disposal and scheduler return/throw revoke suspended captures and
readers, release ownership, and disconnect queued handles from receiver/context/source state.

cannot introduce fresh work during eviction/disposal, and obsolete work cannot erase a newer
request. The renderer scheduler now accepts the required next/return structure; its runtime

## Packed root and description validation — 2026-10-25

The experiment now includes source-bound mdast validation and complete block/outline
cross-checks before the diagnostic receiver's independent fresh parser/render/layout oracle.
The production transport remains unchanged. `validatePackedRoot` rejects unknown node types
and fields, wrong scalar types and child categories, malformed math data, inconsistent source
positions and node/depth excesses. It traverses packed scopes without expanding a native
root. Long math values and outline plaintext compare fixed-workspace streams, preserving
chunk boundaries and undefined progress rather than materializing complete strings.

Sparse line/line-start checkpoints use two Uint32 values per 256 UTF-16 source units.
Construction yields after 4,096 units; position lookup scans at most 255 units. Source
hashing and Unicode character counting also yield after 4,096 units. A source made entirely
of 1 MiB line endings needs **33,032 weighted index bytes**. CR/LF/CRLF checkpoint boundaries,
tabs, astral characters, lone surrogates and paired-surrogate boundaries remain exact.
The pinned parser excludes one initial BOM from offsets and columns. A definition and its
following setext heading can have overlapping source ranges, and GFM literal-autolink
transforms can omit text/link positions. Tests preserve those actual parser conventions;
positioned nodes still require exact coordinates and ancestor bounds. Block hashes match
`describeBlock`'s existing raw-source slice convention, including BOM input. Consumer mapping
for that convention remains integration work.

`validatePackedDescriptions` requires the exact metadata field schema and matching source
hash/parser version. Every positioned block must have its exact ordered kind, range, source
hash and line count. Every outline entry must match the heading's range, depth and streamed
`plainText`, including nested formatting, code, math, links, image alt text and HTML. It
checks exact Unicode character counts and valid timing fields. **Word counts currently get
only integer/type/bounds checks.** Parser equivalence, exact Intl word counts and rendered
HTML/layout validation remain required; this layer is not a complete production validator.

Temporary frame/index workspaces reserve retained and staging capacity before allocation.
Concurrent streams must fit both the local validator budget and aggregate session capacity.
Guarded child paths copy bounded input and expire with their parent item/capture. Scalar-type
and key-count reads avoid decoding long values or copying unknown wide field lists. Validator
handles themselves are capture-owned and charged as readers, including while queued before
the first advance. Revocation closes generators and drops index/source references without
requiring another advance. Reentrant revocation defers generator return until the running
advance unwinds. Completion, failure, return, capture release and disposal close all scopes.

## Exact source-bound document subtree reuse — October 25

`PackedDocumentBaseline.create` independently completes document validation, including exact
word counts, before admitting source-free per-root metadata. It borrows a same-owner capture
and records each immutable root record, source interval, logical nodes/depth, source-dependent
field-length minimum and block/heading cursor intervals. Its cache costs **1,024 bytes per
root plus a fixed/depth reserve**; construction staging ends before persistent retention.
This is a document-consistency certificate, not evidence of a fresh parse or renderer output.

The new root and each candidate's type, parent placement, position kind, line/column/offset
anchors and source bounds still validate. Reuse requires the exact shared immutable record,
only a supported position shift, equal BOM convention and an exact UTF-16 source comparison
in batches of at most **4,096 units**. Both parser coordinates (excluding the initial BOM)
and raw source spelling used by descriptor hashes are covered. Exact source plus valid
anchors proves shifted descendant coordinates without decoding every descendant again.
The cached minimum rechecks every source-dependent string/URL/alignment bound against the
new source length, including the existing seven-unit autolink URL allowance. Changed fields,
overlays, source content, unsupported transforms or incompatible owners fall back to normal
validation. Every reused descendant still counts against current node/depth limits.

Each nested block descriptor and heading is consumed in order from old/new admitted forward
streams. Shared descriptor records require the exact corresponding range shift. Reserialized
descriptors receive exact key/value/range comparison; headings additionally compare complete
text streams and their new source-length bound. Missing/extra/forged metadata rejects. A
backwards baseline cursor falls back before consuming current metadata. Document schema,
source hash/parser binding, timing/count fields and Unicode character counting still run;
the **complete independent whole-document word validation remains unchanged**.

An inspection belongs to both the current validator and the borrowed baseline/capture.
Close, release or disposal clears metadata and cancels active inspections. An explicit
completion value prevents cancellation from appearing as successful EOF. This preserves
receiver commit/ACK ordering. Cache construction closes partial holds/readers on failure;
escaped keys have no arena/source/owner backlink.

## Immutable subtree prose reuse with complete word segmentation — October 25

`PackedWordBaseline.create` first completes the independent exact word validator. It then
admits text-leaf preorder chunks, including the separators between empty leaves, for each
eligible immutable root child. Its private map entries transition from construction plans
to cached output; plans and finished caches do not accumulate in separate collections.
Metadata costs **512 bytes per root plus fixed/depth reserves**. Persistent UTF-16 text is
charged at two bytes per unit, with 128 bytes per conservatively bounded chunk. The complete
largest subtree collector, decoder scratch and traversal frames must also fit before copying.
Cache admission still uses **8 MiB**, and aggregate renderer retention stays **64 MiB**.
Insufficient capacity rejects and releases partial state.

A later same-owner revision can reuse only the exact immutable record with an unchanged
subtree. Position-only shifts preserve prose; text/child overlays and new arena records use
the full traversal/decoder path. Full logical node/depth costs and the maximum text-leaf
length against the current source remain mandatory. Two scans rebuild the exact current
prose in parser order, inserting a space between every pair of text leaves, including empty
ones. Cached inputs are copied in at most **4,098 UTF-16 units per advance**. The complete
prose reservation, final join, **one whole-string `Intl.Segmenter` call**, every word segment
and the comparison with the supplied count remain. No per-block word counts are added.
Multilingual boundaries therefore retain the original parser behavior.

The cache borrows its certified capture; active validation belongs to both that capture and
the new capture. Closing either capture, the cache or the owner revokes work and releases
holds. An explicit inspection-completion value prevents borrowed cancellation from becoming
successful EOF. Escaped cache capabilities contain guarded getters in a source-free factory
frame; after close they cannot retain the private chunk arrays. Direct native chunk access
is internal admitted inspection output and requires separate ownership if retained by a
caller. Closed or incompatible baselines fall back before inspection.

## Independently owned packed preview models — October 25

`PackedSession.own` and capture-bound `own` now admit native output into that exact session's
resource ledger. `PackedValue` stores the native value and its independent hold. Releasing
the handle or disposing the session clears both; closed handles retain neither output nor
an accounting callback. Source-free owner tokens permit an exact same-session check without
retaining a session after closure. Independent holds for the same object/weight share the
resource charge; inconsistent weights and partial capacity failures reject atomically.
Ordinary native objects obtained from a handle remain borrowed: trusted consumers must
drop installed widgets/status and other raw references before releasing their handle.

`preparePackedPreviewInput` completes the existing full snapshot validation and native
measurement/copy, then synchronously exchanges the copy workspace for one independent native
output hold. Successful completion transfers that handle to the caller. Failure/cancellation,
including the final suspension before handoff, releases partial output. Closing the input
capture or evicting the base afterwards leaves successful output usable and charged. The
existing `inspectPackedPreview` uses this path and releases its output when inspection ends.
Its exact input values, mandatory validation and bounded copy staging remain unchanged.

The application now has an experimental `OwnedPackedPreview.prepare` consumer. It checks
the complete authoritative editor `Text` against the source in 4,096-unit steps under a
32 KiB comparison workspace, prepares validated native input, then independently admits the
real occurrence/index/model work before allocating it. The resulting handle owns its input,
widget model, status and occurrence tracker after capture closure/base eviction. It does not
import into the production controller/service. Installed native model/status values require
the same explicit lifetime discipline before handle release or session disposal.

Replacements fork immutable occurrence ranges. Preparing/committing a replacement does not
mutate the installed tracker's state; mapped unchanged widget identities remain exact, even
with duplicate paragraphs. Every resumed preparation step checks the predecessor's version,
and commit checks it again. Edits, release, another replacement commit or namespace changes cannot
silently install a stale replacement. Same-session ownership, document/generation, parser,
renderer/options identity and nondecreasing revisions are mandatory. A failed commit cannot
succeed on a second attempt. Capacity rejection releases the candidate and preserves the
old usable model; it does not establish that every large replacement fits.

Model admission includes **65,536 fixed bytes**, **twice the old/new source lengths**, and
**1,024 bytes per old/new semantic descriptor** for candidate/index/ID/builder/model storage.
The full input also remains independently reserved, including strings/headings shared by
the model/status. These are explicit experiment weights requiring heap calibration, not
portable conservative heap bounds. Existing caps remain **64 MiB aggregate retention / 8 MiB
wire and staging**. The helper has no complete AST or full HTML output.

## Actual widget teardown and native model collection — October 25

CodeMirror may reuse an equivalent widget's DOM with a newer widget object. A per-widget
abort-controller map then misses the controller when that newer object destroys the DOM.
`RenderedWidget` now associates controllers with DOM in a module-level weak map and removes
the entry before aborting. Widget equality also checks kind. Source/link handlers use the
same abort signal and no longer retain the widget through an options lookup on `this`.
Detached DOM cannot continue dispatching source/link actions after its lifetime ends.

A separate heap investigation found that DOMPurify's `removed` diagnostics retained an
attribute's mounted parent tree, including CodeMirror's tile and its native block. The
application's shared sanitizer now clears these unused diagnostics in `finally` after
every markdown, math SVG or diagram sanitization. Sanitization rules are unchanged.

`test/e2e/widget-lifetime.spec.ts` builds an isolated browser fixture and opens it in sandboxed
Electron with context isolation and no Node integration. It imports the actual editor,
experimental `OwnedPackedPreview` and production widget renderer/sanitizer. It introduces
no production bridge, debug hook or packed transport activation. Profiles, build output,
logs, traces and failure-only heap snapshots stay under `test/artifacts/logs/`.

Three browser tests cover equivalent DOM reuse followed by actual removal, kind changes,
exactly-once cancellation, detached source/link handlers, sanitized raw HTML, Source/Live
mode switches, unchanged source/selection/widget IDs and native output collection. The
owned-model test replaces only after Source mode ends every old DOM consumer. Status is
rendered as plain text. Chromium GC collects seven actual old native values (model, blocks
array, two blocks, status, outline array and heading) while the replacement remains usable
and charged by two holds. Its seven values remain alive while installed, then collect
after final DOM/status teardown and handle release. All fourteen watched values collect;
the live session has zero holds/readers and only its 256-byte baseline remains.

The fixture initially retained abort signals to count cancellation. Chromium's default
abort reason carries a stack that can retain the calling widget, making those observations
own the very values being watched. It now records a primitive abort count and weak DOM
references. A subsequent snapshot identified the independent DOMPurify retention described
above; removing that retention makes the actual collection assertions pass.

A reversible negative control restores per-widget controller storage and fails precisely
because final DOM removal leaves `aborted: 0` instead of `1`
(`test/artifacts/logs/.widget-lifetime-negative.log`). The fixed source is restored afterwards. The final
fixture run passes all three tests (`test/artifacts/logs/.widget-lifetime-e2e.log`, artifacts
`test/artifacts/logs/widget-lifetime-e2e/`). Seven production Electron tests for Live Preview, sanitizer
security, isolated diagrams and suspended apply also pass in the ten-test regression run
(`test/artifacts/logs/.widget-lifetime-regression.log`, `test/artifacts/logs/widget-lifetime-regression/`). The final
fixture additionally checks predecessor collection and status ownership after that run.

## Independent widget and asynchronous consumer leases — October 25

`PackedValue.retain()` now opens an independent handle on the same native resource in its
exact session. Native resource bytes are shared by identity; each additional handle still
charges **320 bytes** of ledger metadata and consumes an existing hold slot. Retention,
staging and the **256-hold limit** remain unchanged. Closing a handle clears its value,
hold and fork callback. Retaining a closed/disposed value fails. Failed admission leaves
the original handle usable and does not leak a partial resource reservation.

`OwnedPackedPreview.retain()` returns a `PackedPreviewLease` with model/status getters,
retention and release, without controller map/commit methods. A lease holds both native
input and model state, adding **640 bytes** of handle metadata. It can outlive the controller
handle and can retain another consumer lease. Failure of the second hold rolls back the
first; a test reaches 255 existing holds to verify this exact partial-failure path. Session
disposal revokes handles but cannot revoke escaped JavaScript objects. Trusted consumers
must end every raw borrow first; the browser fixture waits for pending jobs before disposal.

The actual widget renderer accepts an optional transferred consumer lease. DOM cancellation
closes that lease; code, math and image promises independently retain their inputs until
both result/error handlers finish. Cancelled queued code jobs are removed immediately;
running grammar loads keep their charge until they settle. Diagram callbacks and bridge
jobs have separate leases. A cancelled in-flight diagram keeps its bridge lease until both
the render and cancellation IPC promises settle, in either order. Busy replies keep the
job's lease between admission attempts. Synchronous registration/invocation failures release
their leases. A synchronous widget mount failure also aborts its editor lifetime.

The isolated packed browser fixture now transfers these real leases into the production
renderer. Replacing an owned preview while equivalent DOM remains mounted preserves that
DOM and keeps its old model/status charged through DOM leases after the controller handle
releases. Chromium GC verifies all seven old values remain alive, then collect after actual
DOM teardown while the seven replacement values stay usable. The replacement collects
after its own final teardown.

Controlled image loaders resolve or reject after cancellation. All six native model/status
values remain alive and charged by two holds while pending, then collect and leave only
the session's 256 bytes. Controlled diagram bridge promises verify the same behavior when
render or cancellation finishes first, including a rejected render response. These are
lifetime fixtures; the production diagram regression tests still use the real sandbox.

A test delays the actual Python grammar asset selected from Vite's generated manifest.
Four code widgets initially have **18 holds**: controller, four DOM consumers and four
code jobs. Cancellation releases the controller, all DOM consumers and the queued fourth

values remain alive until the asset loads, then collect with zero holds. Another test
delays the real math-worker asset with the existing watchdog clock paused only during that
controlled delay. Its running/queued promises keep **four holds / seven native values**
after DOM cancellation, then settle and release after the real worker resumes. No latency
or watchdog acceptance conclusion is drawn from the paused-clock test.

## Bounded owned preview integration — October 25

transfers independent leases to its real widget renderer. This is renderer-side preparation
after the existing whole-root JSON transfer; MSP2 transport and incremental parsing remain
disabled. No parser node, position, descriptor, heading, count or projection is omitted.

Worker and controller share admission of at most **524,288 source UTF-16 units**, **2,000
semantic descriptors**, and **2,000 root children**. The worker supplies exact serializer
layout only for these candidates, avoiding another full render on the renderer thread.

The controller requires layout before packing and returns to sliced native preparation if
candidate admission or preparation fails. Synchronous encoding/index admission still precedes
cooperative validation; these bounds are a rollout boundary, not proof of a 4 ms maximum.

scheduler continuation, edits while apply is suspended, then verifies only the newest complete
snapshot installs and the exact final source saves.

## Owned serialization of complete packed roots — October 25

`PackedCapture.serialize(path, limits)` now returns cancellable, capture-owned work that
serializes the complete selected value directly from its immutable packed representation.
It preserves every selected value and lazy text/array/position/range transform. It never
collects an ordinary native tree or a long decoded string. A measurement pass determines the
exact output size; a second pass writes one independently owned buffer. Dense record-ID
chunks avoid a native Map entry per record. Ancestor references, schemas, remapping chunks
and string scratch share a reserved workspace. The exact output allocation is admitted
before native allocation, and successful output remains charged after capture/base release.
Cancellation and revocation close partial output and workspace. Invalid or insufficient
node/depth/key/workspace/byte bounds reject without publishing a partial value. Bounds include
128 levels and at most 64 object fields with 1,024-unit names; unsupported input is rejected,
never truncated. Native allocation, bounded schema spelling/hashing and map operations remain
atomic. Working weights still require packaged calibration and are not portable heap bounds.

property names, scalar edge cases, all **65,536 UTF-16 code units**, surrogate/escape boundaries,
long strings without native string reads, old-capture immutability and combined persistent
transforms. They also verify cancellation before start, during measurement, after output
allocation and on capture release; exact owner-stat restoration; actual transfer; path/limit
binding; insufficient limits; allocation admission before invoking ArrayBuffer; and bounded
large-array reference progress. The focused run passes (`test/artifacts/logs/packed-serialize-focused.log`).

## Bounded full resync from committed packed graphs — October 25

`PackedPublisher.offerCurrentSteps` now handles a full response from an exact idle committed
graph after receiver eviction or a lost receipt. It retains that graph, normalizes/binds the
request before suspension, and admits construction/envelope metadata plus actual output in the
same session. An untransformed complete arena can copy its already validated wire encoding
without decoding scalars or building remapping tables: output allocation is admitted first,
copying yields every **64 KiB**, and separate scratch reserves **4,096 bytes**. This copies the
complete encoding, including any unreachable records; it is not pruning/compaction. Persistent
overlays use the measured serializer, with explicit failure when combined capacity is absent.

The publisher holds the output through transfer and an exact acknowledgement. Full resync
does not prepare or commit a duplicate worker graph. Acknowledgement checks exact current
graph identity, including replacement with the same source object; changed/pending/evicted
graphs reject. Cancellation revokes escaped untransferred buffers, releases work/metadata/output
and preserves the committed result. Successful acknowledgement advances the accepted transport
token so later deltas use the receiver's exact accepted base. Mandatory receiver validation
still precedes every acknowledgement. Invalid envelope/schema/limits or capacity never produce
partial acceptance. The application service remains on the existing JSON transport.

The **27 new tests** cover direct byte equality and independent output lifetime, bounded copy
advances, cancellation before/during copy, receiver eviction, real MessagePort transfer,
lost-ACK retry, stale receipts, the next valid delta, prior-capture immutability, queued and
pending graph changes, persistent overlay resync and cancellation during both serializer
passes. They also exercise normalized envelope overflow, invalid copy limits, source/schema
rejection, request/limit binding, concurrent offers, allocation admission under total-capacity
failure with successful retry, and publisher/session disposal in either order. Focused tests

## Packed full-root handoff to translated reading — October 25

The application now consumes packed roots for translated reading from bounded owned previews.
The preview retains an independently charged complete-root capture; reading forks that exact
immutable revision and serializes the selected root cooperatively. Its independently owned
buffer crosses the actual translation Worker with a transfer list. Native preview fallbacks
keep their existing capture path. The main semantic worker/service transport remains JSON.
Keeping a root pin also retains its complete arena under the renderer session's existing
64 MiB allowance; DOM/async widget leases do not keep that root after preview release.

The reading worker counts actual binary plus envelope bytes against 8 MiB, binds source/hash
and parser/renderer versions, and validates the complete mdast schema and source-relative
geometry before native expansion. The validation copy is admitted before allocation, then
exchanged synchronously for arena ownership. Incoming payload/envelope and 8 MiB decoder
staging are reserved against the existing 32 MiB worker allowance. After validation teardown,
native decoding uses the remaining retained budget. Decoded weights are included with the
existing plan/unit/block accounting, and an early plan check precedes asynchronous job
preparation. Invalid/overflowing prepares clear any previous plan. Extraction/reconstruction
still use a native tree inside the worker; total portable heap calibration remains open.

## Bounded renderer traversal batches — October 26

The next initial-validation profile identified scheduler overhead from yielding at every
small native renderer bookkeeping visit. Description, URL-policy traversal, serialization
planning and widget traversal now use a shared `ProjectionTraversalBudget`: at most 16
counted node/property visits or 4,096 text units before yielding. Text counters span adjacent
values rather than resetting per string. Raw strings retain the same lexical progress even
when no escaping is required. Every logical node/depth check and every allocation admission

## Exact unsigned-integer decode without exponentiation — October 26

The packed reader now returns one-byte unsigned integers directly and assembles continued
seven-bit groups with shifts. The final `>>> 0` preserves the complete unsigned 32-bit domain,
including values above the signed boundary. Overflow validation runs before shifting the
fifth group; zero-ending overlong encodings still reject as noncanonical. Truncated values
retain their exact prior cursor/error behavior. This changes no encoding, schema, allocation,
index size, reader lifetime or retained/staging charge.

Five new tests use an independent arithmetic encoder/decoder rather than the production
writer as their primary oracle. They cover every one/two-byte integer, all width/sign
boundaries, every truncation of representative values, every fifth byte, overlong-zero
endings, all 65,536 two-byte prefixes, 20,000 seeded valid values and 20,000 seeded arbitrary
byte sequences. Successful reads leave a sentinel untouched; malformed reads match exact
error and consumed-byte count. Mixed-width sequential reads and forked offset cursors remain
independent. Existing whole-codec malformed record/reference/string tests pass too.

preview preparation now reuses that completed fact for the exact immutable snapshot rather
than repeating the complete walk. Matching requires the actual revision object and owner,
original source object, identical snapshot path, exact render policy and valid budgets at
least as permissive as those originally validated. Equal identity fields alone cannot match.

stricter budgets retain the existing full validation path. Later-revision subtree caches
continue their original checks.

metadata; the existing HTML path supplies the exact snapshot prefix. No separate arena/root
or native graph is retained. Once matched, the preview's own independently live capture keeps
the same revision immutable. Closing the baseline or its borrowed capture afterwards does
not invalidate that completed validation fact and no further baseline data is borrowed.
Closing the preview capture still cancels native work. Native measurement, output admission,
copying and transfer retain their original limits and cleanup.

**64 MiB ownership / 8 MiB staging** limits. No application implementation or production
