Three forced GCs precede each retained checkpoint. During cooperative work, the Node harness
requests `Runtime.getHeapUsage` and waits 20 ms between completed CDP calls; actual cadence
also includes debugger latency. Ownership weights are sampled at task boundaries/completion
to keep the observer from allocating per-advance statistics. Raw V8 used heap, backing storage
and embedder heap are recorded separately. Tables below sum those distinct returned components
and subtract the case's warmed baseline. That sum is a measured subset of process memory.
Periodic maxima include garbage/diagnostic overhead and may miss peaks inside synchronous
calls; they are not physical memory/RSS bounds. Native DOM widgets, semantic producer memory,
loader-worker memory, main-process IPC and aggregate application ownership are outside this
isolated measurement. Base64 export for the independent root comparison occurs only after
the measured serialization checkpoint.

temporary frozen view for each scalar/type/length/key query. The selected node stays local to

resolve the path once before budget admission, preserving the selected value if a caller's

## Composed guarded scope paths — October 26

Previously each child added a closure that recreated its parent views on every read. Atomic
view operations resolve the scope prefix followed by the caller's relative path in one call,
without concatenating a new query array or caching raw nodes/views. Every read still executes
the original capture/item/inspector guard. Child paths keep their existing per-call validation;
sibling selection and missing-path behavior remain unchanged. Iterators and text streams
materialize their independently admitted view once when opened and keep their existing
revocation/cancellation lifetimes. Empty scope query paths share one frozen constant.

## Document absence proofs for projection context scans — October 26

The document baseline's existing full subtree summary pass now records whether each complete
top-level subtree contains no definitions, footnote definitions or footnote calls. This boolean
uses the existing conservative metadata reservation; no extra pass, retained map or admission
increase is introduced. Projection output validation and its definition-cache planning/copying
can reuse the source-free absence metadata only after exact original-source object, actual
immutable revision/owner, document path and valid non-stricter budget checks. Equal identity
fields, other paths/owners/revisions and range overlays cannot supply this proof. Complete
logical node/depth costs are charged even when descendants need no context traversal.

This certifies absence of context contributions, not renderer output. Full document/schema/
geometry and HTML/layout/widget correspondence checks remain. Independent eligibility walks,
cache admission/copying and full root serialization remain. A callback retains the revocable
document handle rather than its metadata map: closing the borrowed baseline restores full
walks, while independently live projection construction can finish. No wire format, ordinary
worker transport, source/output cap or activation rule changes.

## OS process observations beside packed renderer isolate measurements — October 26

`node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-packed-renderer-memory.mjs --process-memory` now runs a separate
minified diagnostic and preserves the ordinary heap/allocation reports. The mode rejects
combination with `--allocations` before starting Electron. A self-contained main-process
sampler queries `app.getAppMetrics()` after each CDP heap query, identifies the measured
window by OS renderer PID and process creation time, and retains every sampled Electron
process row plus simultaneous totals. Electron's documented kilobyte fields are normalized
to bytes; optional private-byte fields remain absent when unavailable. Summaries distinguish
absolute footprints from increases over each case's own baseline. Renderer identity and
duplicate process rows are checked. No application IPC or production instrumentation is added.

Electron documents the fields in
[MemoryInfo](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/memory-info) and
[ProcessMetric](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/process-metric).
Windows private bytes represent private commitment; working sets describe resident pages
and can include shared pages. See Microsoft's
[memory counter mapping](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/memory-performance-information).
Summed working sets therefore do not measure unique physical memory. Process lifetime peak
working sets include startup and warmup; maxima from different processes must not be summed
as though simultaneous. Heap and OS observations are successive, not atomic, and the extra
query changes cadence. Periodic observations can miss peaks. Post-GC checkpoints do not
promise OS decommit, and no new ownership threshold is inferred.

## Fixed-width position intern keys — October 26

The encoder now constructs position intern keys directly from fourteen UTF-16 units: a
two-unit type prefix and two units for each of the six validated uint32 coordinates.
This replaces decimal conversion, comma joining and prefix concatenation for position keys.
The representation is injective over those coordinates, including zero, high bits and
surrogate-valued units. It is internal to the interning map; shape order, record order,
position-record fields, sharing and MSP2 wire bytes remain unchanged. Ordinary array/object
record keys retain their existing representation.

The fixed position key admits **128 bytes** for its spelling/header/copy allowance before
construction, replacing the previous six-reference decimal-key reserve of **448 bytes**.
Unique coordinate arrays, record objects and map entries retain their separate **256-byte**
charge; completed identity entries, logical visits/depth, caller-owned input, other tables,
native enumeration, writer chunks and output admission remain unchanged. Duplicate keys
release their temporary charge. This is a concrete representation change and a corresponding
explicit storage weight, not a measured physical-memory reduction or a new aggregate bound.

## Compact record intern keys — October 26

Ordinary array/object encoder records now intern an exact binary string instead of decimal
child-ID joins. A disjoint `r:` prefix precedes two UTF-16 units for the shape identity
(array maps to zero, object shape IDs to their successor), then two units per uint32 child
ID. Fixed widths preserve ID high/low halves, ordering and arity without delimiter ambiguity;
the prefix separates these records from position intern keys. Shapes that cannot produce a
valid uint32 wire tag reject before key construction. Native `Map` string equality remains
authoritative; no probabilistic hash or collision-based identity replaces it.

One **4,096-unit / 8,192-byte** scratch table, covered by the existing fixed encoder reserve,
is reused across blocks of at most **2,048 child IDs**. Wide records yield after each block,
including their final block before joining. The encoder admits **256 + 16 × references**
before constructing fragments, clears the fragment list after joining, then releases
**8 × references**. A unique key retains **256 + 8 × references** for key/copy allowance and
map/record metadata; duplicate keys release the remainder. The separately admitted reference
array, completed-object table, position keys, caller input and writer/output charges remain
unchanged. Final joining/map lookup, shape JSON spelling, native enumeration and final
output allocation remain atomic. These are explicit live weights, not physical measurements.

## Direct record emission during encoding — October 26

The encoder no longer stores a second complete native record graph until final emission.
Unique scalars, positions and completed array/object records now emit directly into bounded
body chunks in their original intern-ID order. Only the current traversal frames retain
child-ID arrays; finishing a frame releases that array's charge. Unique position coordinates
are emitted immediately and discarded, with only their exact intern key/map entry retained.
The actual unique position-entry charge drops from 256 to **128 bytes** because no retained
coordinate array/record object remains. Ordinary record-key admission still reserves
**256 + 16 × references** during construction, releases **8 × references** after clearing
fragments and another **128 bytes** on unique insertion because the native record object
is absent. Scalar map admission retains its existing conservative weight.

The root ID is resolved and emitted before clearing scalar/record/shape lookup maps and
replacing the completed-identity WeakMap. Only after those references are dropped does the
ledger release their accumulated charge. Shape lists retain their independently admitted
storage and spelling allowance. A separate header writer receives exactly the body's
remaining byte allowance. `finishSteps(prefix)` admits one combined buffer before allocation
and copies header then body at 64 KiB source-chunk boundaries. Both source writers' chunks
remain charged through final copying; their backing buffers are not treated as freed early.
Header, body and root footer share the original actual wire-byte cap. Capacity/cancellation
publishes no partial result. Native joining, shape spelling, enumeration and output
allocation remain atomic; caller-owned input and aggregate/native physical memory remain
separate requirements.

under ignored `/test/artifacts/logs/`.

entries**, at the existing **96-byte-per-entry** weight. On rotation it drops the old
WeakMap before releasing that charge, then admits the next entry. Scalar/record value
interning remains complete and authoritative, preserving the exact original record ID when
an evicted object is traversed again. Active ancestors remain in a separate WeakSet for cycle
detection. The root is always recorded after its final rotation before resolving its ID.
Current memo charges remain part of the intern total released before final output, without
double releasing previous rotations.

This is a bounded acceleration cache. Revisiting an evicted identity can traverse its
children again and consume more of the unchanged node/depth/work allowance. Highly shared
graphs may therefore reject earlier on traversal admission; that is not an exemption from
the limits or a physical peak guarantee. The two-argument byte-only experimental encoder
keeps its previous identity-memo behavior. MSP2 spelling, record/shape order, scalar and

## Exact typed encoder record index — October 26

The encoder now interns position and array/object records through a typed hash index over
already emitted immutable body bytes. Each slot stores the full hash, ID plus one and body
offset. A matching hash is only a candidate: exact tag, array length and all uint32 values
must match before reusing the record. Native record-key strings, fragments and their maps
are no longer retained. Scalar and shape interning retain their existing exact behavior.
The MSP2 header/body spelling and complete semantic values remain unchanged.

Tables stay at most half full. A growing table is admitted before allocation with the old
table still charged; cooperative rehashing commits the new table only when complete. A
cancelled or failed rehash releases the candidate table while preserving existing lookups.
Explicit construction limits cap collision probes at 256 slots. The byte-only codec retains
its previous contract. Hashing and exact comparison yield every 256 values, and rehashing
yields every 256 old slots or probes. Shape spelling/map lookup and native enumeration remain
atomic; enumeration admission still follows the native allocation. Caller-owned input and
aggregate physical memory calibration remain open.

The archived pre-position-key codec remains an independent wire oracle, SHA-256
`5037D9F2BFFA49474DAF2D9353F3A8DDF76076FA7D123E6CB0D757B138FA6CE7`.
`node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-packed-encoder-budget.mjs --baseline` passes all **1,304 CommonMark
comparisons** in both grammars and exact same-input wire/decode equality for all complete
diagnostic snapshots. Current report `test/artifacts/logs/packed-encoder-budget.json` records
**2026-10-26T13:16:36.261Z**, log `test/artifacts/logs/record-index-profile.log`. The preceding implementation
and report are preserved in `test/artifacts/logs/packed-record-index-baseline/`; the report records
**2026-10-26T12:54:02.170Z**. These are explicit construction weights, not measured heap bytes.
The large diagnostic allowance quantifies the whole model; the separate product-sized attempt
keeps **32 MiB / 800,000 visits / depth 512**.

## Streaming packed translation extraction — October 26

`packages/translate/src/packed-extract.ts` adds an internal experimental complete-root
consumer stage. It validates the entire source-bound packed root, including ineligible later
branches, before exposing any translation unit. It then copies and projects only one
paragraph, heading or table cell at a time. Source-relative ranges, semantic child paths,
privacy bindings, grouped HTML, token limits, oversized-unit errors, occurrence-ID uniqueness
and logical aggregate limits share the native extractor's `UnitExtraction` and
`projectTranslationUnit` implementations. Native extraction's traversal and public return
shape remain unchanged.

The source/capture identity must match the same `PackedSource` resource. The existing
800k-node / depth-128 complete validator remains mandatory. Each native unit and projection
workspace stays reserved through inspector suspension; the occurrence-ID set stays reserved
through the complete traversal. Before projection the local reservation includes 2 MiB plus
twice the admitted native unit size, alongside traversal/identity/native-copy costs. Results
retain only counts and weighted peaks. The trusted callback must independently admit any
unit, private binding or output it retains after returning. This API does not yet retain a
translation plan, expose a complete native root, or route production reading through it.

## Persistent packed translation plans and complete revocation — October 26

`packages/translate/src/packed-plan.ts` adds an internal persistent plan on top of the
complete-root unit extractor. It independently pins the exact immutable revision and retains
only frozen occurrence metadata and canonical provider-safe payloads. Complete native roots,
private native subtrees and bindings are absent from persistent plan storage. An ordered
`inspectUnits` scan rehydrates each unit's private bindings on demand, validates its metadata
and payload against the frozen occurrence, and keeps transient reservations live throughout
callback suspension. Scanning avoids random full child-path lookups on wide roots. Source,
schema, position geometry, unit identity and logical aggregate limits remain checked.

The caller provides a persistent metadata allowance inside its total retained budget. That
entire allowance is removed from the extractor's local ceiling, while the shared session
also charges source/arena and concurrent captures. `ExtractionMemory` now has an optional
enclosing admission callback, invoked before interning or storing metadata; native callers
without the callback keep their existing behavior. Frozen canonical payloads can be shared
by occurrences whose protected private nodes differ. `prepareCanonicalTranslation` accepts
the structural read-only payload view it uses, allowing these plans to produce identical
provider jobs without needing a native root. Job/hash copies still need caller admission.
The typed iterator return on `PackedWork` now preserves its result type through `yield*`.

The original parent capture can close and the session can publish a later revision while
the plan keeps the previous exact source/root usable. Plan release revokes queued/suspended
inspections. Session disposal or prepared-candidate revocation also closes the plan and
clears its private metadata fields, even when callers retain the closed plan handle. The
units getter is a trusted raw borrow: consumers must end such borrows before release or
independently admit retained output. This is the same limitation as other independently
admitted native values; ordinary JavaScript objects cannot be revoked after escape.

A failing-inspector cancellation test exposed an existing capture cleanup defect: an
exception from a generator's `finally` stopped release before later queued work, workspaces
and the revision pin were closed. `finishPackedCleanup` now completes remaining revocation
before rethrowing the first failure. Capture release clears its owner callback before
running nested cleanup so recursive plan release cannot unpin it early. Session invalidation,
eviction, disposal and prepared discard finish all cleanup phases on failure. A failed
prepared commit closes every inspection, invalidates the candidate and preserves the old
current revision instead of publishing it. Tests check original-error identity, queued work,
independent output holds, sibling prepared forks, exact reader/staging restoration and
zero retained bytes after disposal. No cleanup exception is silently converted to success.

`test/artifacts/logs/verify-packed-plan.mjs` compares native extraction and complete persistent plans,
then compares every rehydrated private unit/binding against its native oracle. Report

all CommonMark examples in both grammars, eight extension cases, 400 generated combinations
and both complete nested roots. Complete nested source/root hashes and the **2,793,561-byte**

## Save synchronizes pending source input before capture (2026-10-27)

A deterministic Electron regression now reproduces a save-ordering defect: a native Save
command can capture the old editor state while a DOM text mutation is waiting for the
editor's input observer. The test delays mutation delivery, selection-change delivery and
layout, while preserving native `takeRecords()` behavior. With the synchronization line
removed, Save reports **All changes saved** but the file lacks the appended ` pending 世界`.
With the fix, Save waits, writes the exact complete text, and undo still restores the
original content. This establishes the pending-input defect independently; it does not
prove that it caused the earlier intermittent 5 MiB source-stress failure.

`SourceInputSynchronization` waits for CodeMirror's public measurement callback, before
which CodeMirror flushes pending DOM input. Document saves await that boundary before
capturing both text and revision. Concurrent waits share a request; unmount/disposal settles
pending waits and ignores late callbacks. The implementation neither accesses private
observer APIs nor serializes editor DOM. All save actions use the same capture path.
Mounted saves now include a measurement boundary before file I/O.

`test/e2e/save-input.spec.ts` drives the actual native command IPC path and verifies pending-input
admission, exact file content, saved status and undo. The negative-control build fails the
exact-content assertion; the fixed build passes the identical test in **1.2 seconds**.

source in `finally` and rebuilds the fixed application afterward.

## Packed-plan translation projection and sequenced reading (2026-10-27)

`PackedTranslationPlan.inspectProjection` now owns a revocable projection inspector. It
retains admitted occurrence indexes, translation statuses and canonical output strings,
and validates outputs in original occurrence order, preserving logical aggregate limits.
It re-creates a unit's private bindings only when a separately admitted exact native block
or footnote context is rendered. Binding construction and reconstruction scratch have
their own shared-session workspace; the inspector releases it and clears the projection
on completion, cancellation, plan release or session disposal. Equal output strings are
interned to one retained value and charged before retention. Provider-safe metadata never
gains native bindings. Trusted native inputs must come from the same validated revision.

`ReadingSequence` converts one source block and its translated copy at a time, retaining
row contents/anchors and widget slots rather than complete mdast/HAST trees. Public
`ProjectionSequence` state now supports the same child substitution as whole-root
projection, including table cells and footnote bodies. First definitions, repeated/cyclic
footnote calls, language labels and per-language export-slot numbering span the full
sequence. The ordinary renderer and sequence share reading decoration and export-slot
policy. Complete raw HTML fragments stay concatenated; they are never published as
independently parsed indexed rows. Replacement and bilingual rows share repeated contents
while retaining each occurrence's anchor. Closing a sequence drops its state and callbacks.

`reading-sequence.test.ts` compares sequence output against independent whole-root
reconstruction for all **652 CommonMark examples in both grammars**, every reading layout
and three indexing thresholds. Additional fixtures cover mixed missing/invalid translations,
private code/URLs, table cells, list tightness, Unicode/CRLF, unused/duplicate/cyclic notes,
raw HTML spanning blocks, math and diagrams. A 1,000-paragraph repeated fixture checks
complete row contents and occurrence anchors. Reservation rejection makes partial sequences
unusable instead of reusing altered footnote/slot state.

`packed-reading-sequence.test.ts` composes actual packed context/block reads, persistent
plans, borrowed projections and sequenced reading. It compares complete results and
statuses against native extraction/reconstruction for all **1,304 CommonMark/grammar
combinations**, a combined extension/privacy case and both complete **1 MiB nested** roots.
All three layouts match. The nested test explicitly rejects a complete native root copy
under the unchanged **8 MiB staging** allowance, then succeeds by reading individual blocks.
The row output allowance remains **24 MiB**. An initial replacement collector retained
unique anchor HTML per row and exceeded that allowance; storing shared contents separately
from anchors fixes the failure without increasing the allowance or truncating output.

These tests admit packed metadata, contexts, native block copies and reconstruction in
the session. Their native oracle, HAST construction and serialization are test-owned:
they establish complete compatibility, **not** a bound on total runtime physical memory.
Production reading adoption still requires simultaneous admission of context, reconstruction,
HAST construction, policy/serialization scratch and persistent output. This new internal path
is not exported through package entry points and does not activate production transport.

## Production packed-reading ownership checkpoint — 2026-10-27

The `prepare-packed` branch now runs `PackedReadingProcessor` in the real reading worker.
The transferred buffer becomes its validated arena, and its persistent translation plan
contains canonical provider-safe payloads and occurrence metadata. It does not retain a
complete native mdast root or every unit's private bindings. Ordinary `prepare` retains its
existing native implementation; semantic transport/admission remains whole-root JSON.

Preparation admits envelope metadata, compact block descriptors, native/shared public unit
records and hashing/job scratch. Cancellation during asynchronous hashing keeps ownership
until settlement, prevents publication of cleared plans and rejects overlapping operations.
Renderer versions, original option stamps, source geometry and full schema remain validated.
Reading can reproject a different raw-HTML policy or localized footer labels from that same
validated mdast source, with no captured HAST/policy reuse.

Each completed language conversion replaces its dead handler/reconstruction scratch with
measured live HAST. Both source and target HAST remain charged together through policy,
decoration and serialization. This fixes dense protected-text staging failure without raising
the **32 MiB worker / 8 MiB staging/message/projection** caps or truncating source/units.
Complete output transfers the existing workspace into a capture-revocable handle; no second
output allocation or uncharged handoff is required. The worker retains output/descriptors
while admitting response clone scratch and calling actual `postMessage`. Publication success,
clone failure, cancellation and disposal release the corresponding response ownership.
Trusted local `execute` results are borrows through the next operation or clear; the wrapper
uses `respond` so publication finishes within ownership.

## Whole-source GFM tokenizer checkpoint — 2026-10-27

The native semantic producer remains on the complete remark/micromark pipeline. The core
parser now omits impossible GFM email/table tokenizer attempts using four immutable processor
variants. They retain the same GFM mdast transforms, frontmatter, math and every other
construct. Public extension records are cloned; shared construct maps and the full processor
remain unchanged. This adds no dependency patch and changes no resource or latency limit.

An email candidate retains the full tokenizer whenever the source contains `@`, an entity
marker or an escape. A table candidate retains it for a pipe, `:-`, `-:`, an entity marker or
an escape. In the pinned tokenizer, a successful pipe-free delimiter needs an alignment
colon immediately adjacent to a hyphen; otherwise it is rejected. Pipe-free aligned
single-column tables therefore still parse as tables. Plain unaligned setext/thematic-break
syntax stays unchanged. CommonMark and non-GFM paths do not perform these extra scans.

## Native postprocessing phase checkpoint — 2026-10-27

The previous replay optimization is retained. The next investigation measures the complete
event graph between native postprocessing passes, rather than inferring physical savings
from end-of-parse compaction or cumulative allocation. A new reproducible diagnostic is
`test/benchmark/profiles/profile-parser-phases.mjs`:

```sh
node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-parser-phases.mjs
node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-parser-phases.mjs --development
node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-parser-phases.mjs --natural
node test/benchmark/profiles/profile-parser-phases.mjs --development --natural
```

Each run launches a fresh Node process. Independent original-source reconstruction verifies
the installed patched sources, and load hooks instrument only the requested default or
development exports. Exact loaded paths are checked. No installed source is written. The
private `fromMarkdown` expression is split into block-tokenized, postprocessed, compacted and
compiled checkpoints. Only its complete event array is observed: CommonMark content resolvers
also subtokenize small child arrays during block parsing, which are excluded. The initial
unscoped prototype sampled those small arrays repeatedly and was stopped; its partial output
is preserved in `test/artifacts/logs/parser-phase-live-graph-unscoped.log`. The corrected initial prototype
and `test/artifacts/logs/parser-phase-live-graph.json` inform the permanent tool.

descriptors**. Completion requires zero pending content events and compaction requires zero
event slots retained through contexts. Reports include runtime versions, source hashes,
baseline memory, event/context counts, pending-content counts and process memory endpoints.
The runtime is **Node 24.18.1**, not the packaged Electron isolate.

## Native event-span compilation checkpoint — 2026-10-27

The native parser now compiles complete event spans after full block tokenization, avoiding
the simultaneous complete postprocessed event graph for documents with separable top-level
structure. This is one complete native parse. All document-wide definitions are known before
inline resolution. Span boundaries require balanced token depth and no outstanding forward
token links. A first prototype cut at container depth alone and failed on a flow chain that
crossed an outer container boundary; `test/artifacts/logs/parser-span-compile-failed-boundary.log` and its
candidate source preserve that failure. Tracking forward links across all tokens corrects
the boundary. Connected flow chains are never split.

Each span is postprocessed completely and list-prepared, then sent through one persistent
root, compiler data, stack, token stack and listener/config context. Transforms execute once
after all spans, with final root endpoints from the complete flattened event stream. Consumed
private block-event slots and prepared/span arrays are released. The generator closes its
arrays and link set on completion or abrupt closure. Public micromark event arrays and
contexts retain their existing contract. This is synchronous event compilation, not source
fragment parsing, incremental edit parsing or a cooperative scheduling guarantee.

The frozen application processors explicitly opt in through `_manuslipEventSpans`. The
general parser retains the original compiler and global future-list preparation ordering.
The private compiler is generated from the exact pinned compiler's list/event loops, and
the application's CommonMark/GFM/frontmatter/math extension set is its compatibility scope.
Changing that extension set requires revisiting cross-span dependencies; other configurations
keep the general path until equivalence is verified. One container or linked flow can cover
the whole source, so there is no hard span or physical memory bound. Semantic wire/source/
node/block/cache limits remain unchanged; packed semantic transport is not activated.

## Projection chunk validation checkpoint — 2026-10-27

Packed snapshot equivalence validation now consumes complete serialized HTML in bounded
chunks. It retains the full admitted native block, HAST, description/policy plan and global
definition/footnote state. Its serialization reservation includes all shallow element shells,
metadata and bounded text scratch, while joined body and widget HTML are absent from this
path. Existing function inspectors continue to borrow fully admitted native outputs. Both
modes share the same preparation and native handler/state pipeline.

The public pinned `hast-util-to-html` still spells attributes, properties, entities and
HTML/SVG shells. Text inputs to native escaping are at most **4,096 UTF-16 units**, and
every output piece is at most that size. Default mandatory entity semicolons preserve exact
boundary spelling. The stream reproduces script/style context, schema transitions, template
content and void-element content rules. Shell calls have cooperative barriers while
unwinding deep lookahead, and chunks yield even when the inspector completes synchronously.
Shell/attribute serialization and native block/HAST construction remain atomic; a bounded
piece size does not establish a wall-time bound for those operations.

The receiver still checks every HTML unit, each visible/invisible layout span and exact
footer boundary, widget kind/range/value/HTML, final widget uniqueness/completeness and
global renderer state. Widget selection preserves the native postorder Map's final value
for repeated source ranges, including code/pre overwrites. Same-length body/widget/footer
forgeries and omitted widgets remain rejected before ACK. No source, wire, session, staging,

## Producer admission, idle dependencies and Worker host — 2026-10-27

**Progress checkpoint; full delivery and packed transport activation remain incomplete.**
Dependency construction now runs as capture-owned cooperative work, including bounded
source bracket scans, node traversal, reference resolution and footnote call ordering.
The existing synchronous API drains the same implementation. Before growth, the application
reserves metadata and scratch in its unchanged producer session; complete source ownership
is already charged. On completion, the temporary reservation transfers synchronously into
an independent index resource hold. Capture release, cancellation and supersession close
active readers and discard partial metadata. Native identifier decoding/case conversion and
array freezing remain atomic; this is local weighted admission, not aggregate physical proof.

Optional `PackedSemanticProducer.cacheSteps()` warms only acknowledged idle data. It never
commits or acknowledges an offer. New valid work cancels partial warmup; invalid prepare/ACK
input preserves it. Repeated warmup reuses the exact current source index. Optional capacity
and unsupported geometry return false without replacing accepted data. Cold incremental
construction uses the same cooperative admitted builder. Complete advanced dependency
provenance still becomes accepted only after the matching transferred result's exact ACK.

`PackedProducerHost` adds the application Worker scheduler over that producer: one current
task, one deferred callback and two-millisecond batches. Supersession releases obsolete work
without leaving it captured by queued callbacks. It enforces complete buffer transfer before
ACK and cancels temporary ownership on scheduling, work or channel failure. Disposal also
releases port callbacks. Its fixed 4,096-byte control allowance shares the 16 MiB producer
session. Per-advance diagnostic measurements are disabled by default. The actual Electron
Worker fixture now uses the host. The ordinary worker/service/controller still uses JSON.

Receiver optimizations preserve complete validation: paired valid descriptor stream items
return directly, discarded-prefix advances still yield, and small immutable numeric range
shapes use bounded direct field lookup. Wide objects retain their cooperative scan and exact
ordering/overflow/underflow checks. No retained weights, wire/session/source/staging ceilings,
fixtures or performance assertions change.

The final suite passes all **1,373 producer/host tests**. The host's **18 tests** cover real
transfers and full native output over repeated deltas, exact/late ACKs, queued/running
supersession and cancellation, bounded scheduling under 30 superseding requests, partial

## Exact snapshot certificates for application consumers (2026-10-27)

The packed receiver now creates an independently owned certificate only after complete
document/projection/layout validation. `PackedCapture.revisionWitness()` supplies a weak
identity predicate for the actual immutable revision and session owner, so an inspection's
revocation at commit does not invalidate an established fact. Certificate data stores bounded
policy/path/limit metadata and no strong revision, arena, source or inspection reference.
The certificate's handle remains charged in its owning session and each consumer separately
retains its graph capture. Merely matching a source hash or revision identity is insufficient.

The receiver, renderer port and `SemanticService` lend the certificate with the capture during
synchronous notification. `DocumentPreview` retains both through sliced native preparation,
then releases temporary ownership. `preparePackedPreviewInput` can reuse complete validation
only for the exact graph, source object, snapshot path, serialized render policy (including
property order), and non-stricter valid limits. A mismatch or closed certificate falls back
to complete validation. Native descriptor/model output still needs its full separate admission.
The ordinary browser factory still uses JSON. No admission weights, caps, corpus or latency
targets were reduced to pass a gate.

## Native candidate lifetime and receiver cache reclamation (2026-10-27)

Native occurrence preparation separates the permanent model reservation from the old
immutable ranges borrowed by its candidate fork. The original source/descriptor weights
remain unchanged and both reservations are admitted before construction. Controller and
read-only leases share the old-range reservation. Successful commit replaces those ranges
and releases that reservation; abandoned/rejected candidates retain it through the last
read-only lease. An independent old installed consumer keeps its own admitted model.
Partial retain failure, cancellation before handoff, owner disposal and repeated release
are covered without invalidating an older accepted model.

That lifetime change reclaims about 2 MiB per committed edited model in the complete corpus,
but alone still leaves the many-small-block second edit requiring full resync. Diagnostic-only
admission instrumentation identifies the actual failure: `validateWordSteps` requests
**6,435,432 bytes** with **4,435,170 bytes** available, at **62,673,694 retained bytes**.
The failed reservation includes a complete prose/join/Intl workspace, alongside the still
retained optional word cache. Source-free weights, counters and stack are in
`test/artifacts/logs/candidate-storage-admission-profile.json`; the preceding candidate-only
run is archived in `test/artifacts/logs/candidate-storage-service-profile.json`.

The receiver now closes the failed validation inspection, reclaims only optional cached
prose, and retries complete snapshot validation once on the same prepared graph. Document
and projection caches remain available. Full text traversal and whole-string Intl word
counting still run. Forged counts fail and cancellation withholds publication/ACK. A second
capacity failure uses the existing full-resync path. No cap, admission weight, semantic check,
fixture or performance target is reduced, and no second payload is requested by this retry.

array segment: its opaque arena token, array record, exact coverage, position/range offsets,
minimum/maximum position offsets, expanded visits and maximum container depth. A later shift

checks. Reused segments yield before publication. Full semantic, output, span, widget and
word-count checks remain mandatory.

## Reuse complete validation during projection cache construction — 2026-10-27

Cold renderer CPU sampling identified a second complete snapshot validation during optional
projection-cache construction. The receiver had already validated that exact immutable
snapshot before ACK/publication. `PackedProjectionBaseline.create` now accepts the existing
`PackedSnapshotCertificate` and reuses completed validation only after checking its private
factory brand, exact graph/owner/source/path, serialized renderer policy and compatible
limits. Closed certificates, different graphs/owners/paths/policies and stricter limits run
full validation. Metadata construction, admission, logical traversal bounds and revocation
still run normally; no native tree/HAST/HTML is cached by this change.

`PackedSnapshotCertificate.validates` checks the private brand and calls the sealed intrinsic
authorization method, rather than a caller-supplied instance method. Its constructor and
prototype are frozen. Preview preparation uses the same check. Prototype copies with forged
authorization methods cannot bypass either consumer's complete validation. The certificate
continues to contain independently charged source-free metadata and a weak revision witness;
it does not pin a graph or source on behalf of another consumer.

work starts after publication and can run before that observation, so observed readiness can
include optional cache work. Earlier blanket statements that this diagnostic excluded idle

## Explicit stack for native copy construction — 2026-10-27

`copyPackedNative` now uses one generator with an explicit object/array frame stack, instead
of one recursively delegated generator per value. This reduces delegation through deeply
nested copies during mandatory projection validation. Frames stay within the existing
depth/workspace reservation. All allocations retain their prior charges and admission order;
there is no new cache or global table. Arrays and discarded prefixes still forward progress,
text collectors still yield at lexical boundaries, and at most sixteen new value visits
share a batch. Object fields retain the 64-key and 1,024-unit per-key bounds and safe own
property definitions, including `__proto__`. Aliased occurrences still count independently.

Each open array iterator closes from the inside out on completion, cancellation or failure.
Cleanup continues if one close throws, including thrown `undefined`; an existing body failure
is preserved. Frames are cleared on exit. Positions reuse the guarded reader's already
complete frozen native result instead of allocating another identical outer object. They
contain numeric values only and retain no arena/view/source references. Measured preflight
still runs its complete traversal before copying; incremental construction still admits
every complete value before allocating it. Inspectors receive output only after full success.

`npm run check` passes **588 linted files**, **579 formatted files**, all runtime boundaries,
four pinned patches and typechecking. Targeted Biome checking passes all four changed code/
script files. `npm test` passes **11,000 tests**, one intentional skip across **164 files**
in **61.53 seconds**. Focused native inspection passes **76 tests**. Eight added cases cover
deep mixed containers and sibling paths, exact expanded alias node/depth limits, the
sixteen-scalar bound and cleanup of five nested arrays when an inner close throws an error
or `undefined`, for both measured and incremental inspection. Evidence:
`test/artifacts/logs/native-copy-stack-check.log`, `test/artifacts/logs/native-copy-stack-final-biome.log`,
`test/artifacts/logs/native-copy-stack-units.log` and `test/artifacts/logs/native-copy-stack-focused.log`.

## Observe process memory through the actual semantic application path — 2026-10-27

The preceding goal turn made implementation and verification progress. The separate root
log-cleanup request found the root already clear; it did not change runtime state. This
checkpoint addresses the next admission evidence gap: previous process measurements used
a diagnostic native producer and loader rather than the real persistent application Worker,
renderer port, service, mounted CodeMirror and Live consumer together.

`test/benchmark/profiles/profile-semantic-service.mjs --process-memory` now measures that actual path.
`test/benchmark/helpers/semantic-service-memory.mjs` samples Electron main-process metrics, normalizes KiB
to bytes and checks renderer PID/creation-time continuity. The driver pauses 20 ms after
completed samples; it does not poll the renderer or force GC during work. Optional fixture

## Schedule optional receiver caches at background priority — 2026-10-27

The actual-path memory checkpoint showed the first observed ready event already had all
three optional caches. `PackedSemanticPort` scheduled warmup through the mandatory receipt
runtime, whose boosted `scheduler.yield` continuation could run cache construction before
ordinary queued observations. Optional receiver cache slices now use
`scheduler.postTask(..., { priority: 'background' })`. Mandatory receipt/preview work retains
its existing scheduler and slice target. Runtimes without background scheduling use their
existing defer method; the browser fallback uses timers. A scheduling rejection can fall
back before execution, but a thrown callback is surfaced without retrying completed work.

The port owns one revocable callback slot per priority. A delayed background callback can
never take a newer mandatory receipt. Slots read current work only when invoked and clear
on cancellation/failure/termination, so obsolete callbacks do not retain old generators.
At most one callback per priority can remain queued. Existing session admission, independent
consumers, complete validation, ACK ordering and cache contents are unchanged.

callback failure without duplicate execution, mandatory receipt with an obsolete background
callback still queued, and active background cancellation/termination/failure. The two

source ACL when the descriptors differ. Exact final SDDL equality remains mandatory; no

## Close suspended work when owner cancellation cleanup fails — 2026-10-27

PackedWork.return previously revoked its owner before calling the suspended generator's
return method. If the owner callback threw, generator cleanup never ran. The handle was
already closed, so holding it or calling return/next again could not recover that cleanup.
The fix invokes generator return from a finally block after immediate owner revocation.
Reentrant cancellation still defers generator return until the running advance unwinds.
The normal next implementation, checkpoints and resource charges are unchanged. Cleanup
exceptions keep the same precedence as the existing next path: a generator cleanup error
can supersede an owner cleanup error.

now verify synchronous resource release with the closed handle held and unadvanced, owner
and generator error precedence, and one-time cleanup. Full static checks pass: 596 linted
files, 587 format-checked files, runtime boundaries, all four pinned parser patches and
TypeScript. **11,078 unit tests in 167 files pass**, with one intentional skip.

## Reject isolated arena tag-query optimizations — 2026-10-27

Two complete arena-query prototypes were measured and reverted. The existing Windows
application and installer remain unchanged. This is evidence for choosing the next
performance change; it does not close a delivery gate.

The first prototype reads the first tag byte for scalar/array/position checks after full
arena validation. Canonical tags 0–7 occupy one byte, and every object tag starts above 7;
shape lookup still decodes the complete varint. No storage or validation is removed.
Five alternating fresh Node pairs measure native-copy medians 198.3739/194.5771 ms
(baseline/candidate), with cumulative sampled allocations 753,747,200/752,422,256 bytes.
Five fresh mounted minified Electron pairs measure cold receipt medians 1440.1/1428.2 ms
(0.8% lower, only 3/5 pairs lower) and first-edit readiness 505.4/505.0 ms. Two receipt
pairs regress, one by 38.3 ms. This does not establish a reliable application improvement.

The second prototype adds a fully admitted Uint8Array kind table, charging 48 bytes plus
one byte per record before allocation. Objects normalize to kind 8; full object tags
remain decoded for shape lookup. It avoids cursor seeks for metadata-only type queries.
Node copy medians are 196.8365/192.2243 ms, with sampled allocations
751,163,448/750,751,608 bytes. Application receipt medians are 1428.7/1413.1 ms
(1.1% lower, 4/5 pairs lower); first edits are 500.8/502.2 ms (slower). The independent
application ledgers add approximately 362,048 retained bytes. Their per-pair differences
also include a few bytes from variable timing-scalar encoding. An exact fixed-data probe
confirms the added table costs 48 + record count, with identical staging. The extra index
and its construction are not retained for this small, mixed application result.

Each experiment substitutes its actual source in both renderer and Worker builds and
checks emitted markers and complete bundle hashes. All 20 native application revisions
per experiment match the separate full six-fixture oracle run, with counts, outlines,
three caches, full/delta behavior and fixed limits intact. Each Node pair verifies complete

physical peak memory or packaged performance acceptance.

A temporary regression covers 260 distinct shapes crossing object tags 128 and 256.
The charged-index focused run passes 701 tests. A separate source-substituted probe runs
all three versions (restored, byte-tag, kind-index), rejects 2,860 wrong-kind calls each,
preserves field/scalar queries and invalid-ID errors, and verifies exact index accounting.
After restoration, all 700 original focused tests pass. Runtime and test sources match
the current ASAR byte for byte; the previous complete package/release verifier passes
again. Its 11,081 unit tests, 73 packaged flows, 154 lifetime probes and actual installer
restoration/removal remain the unchanged release's existing evidence, not new executions.

## Preserve replacements during synchronous Worker failure — 2026-10-27

SemanticService now binds each start call to the exact running request that it installed.
A Worker adapter can synchronously report failure while registering listeners or posting.
That notification can already create a replacement and its newer request. The older call
now returns before scheduling a watchdog or posting its stale request, and its catch only
reports failure while its original request still runs. No scheduling delay, timeout,
restart quota, source fidelity, transport limit or memory-accounting weight changes.

This fixes two independently reproduced recovery errors. A port reporting failure and
then throwing from post previously caused the old catch to terminate the healthy
replacement, consuming another restart allowance. With three real reported failures it
could terminate the fourth, healthy Worker and pause. Listener registration reporting
failure synchronously previously sent replacement request sequence 2 followed by stale
sequence 1, and could leave a stale watchdog. New tests require only the replacement's
request, complete latest output, healthy reuse and no later spurious watchdog restart.

one/three consecutive report-then-throw ports, synchronous message/failure registration,
and the actual PackedSemanticPort throwing from its channel send. The integration case

heading values and zero final ownership. Focused before/after results are 5 failed /

preserved under test/artifacts/logs/service-recovery-before/, test/artifacts/logs/service-recovery-candidate.ts and
test/artifacts/logs/service-recovery-{before,after}-integration.log.

Three bounded source variants were measured and rejected. The current runtime, all
workspace/runtime inputs and the existing Windows installer remain byte-identical to
the preceding serialization-stack release. No limit, fixture, scheduling checkpoint,
transport eligibility or admission weight changed. This turn adds evidence and removes
these hypotheses from the next implementation step; it does not claim a new runtime fix.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inline root visits in the existing depth stack | 212.7 / 198.4 ms | 1,381.4 / 1,389.0 ms | 576.4 / 593.0 ms | Reject: isolated gain does not improve the application |
| Use adjacent sparse checkpoints for coordinate ranges | 227.1 / 302.0 ms | 1,439.1 / 1,431.7 ms | 589.9 / 610.6 ms | Reject: isolated regression and mixed application timing |
| Check for a following checkpoint before that lookup | 206.6 / 194.3 ms | 1,439.5 / 1,412.6 ms | 563.6 / 579.3 ms | Reject: modest cold gain with worse edit median |

Each row uses five alternating fresh minified Electron application pairs with the actual
Worker, receiver, SemanticService, mounted editor and independent full native oracle.
All 30 runs/60 complete native revisions pass, use one Worker, preserve full-then-delta
transport and have no captured Worker errors. Both emitted renderer variants are checked;
the producer imports neither changed helper, and its Worker bytes are identical within
every pair. Cold paired observations improve in 3/5, 4/5 and 4/5 pairs respectively; edit
observations improve in 2/5 pairs for each coordinate variant. The timing variation does
not establish a general application gain, so none of these bodies is shipped. No extra
repeats were taken to seek a passing performance result.

Isolated runs include three warm traversals per variant and a separate sampled-allocation
run, rather than repeated physical memory measurements. Every root profile validates

The coordinate idea derives positions from the next existing sparse checkpoint when
an interval contains at most one line ending or the offset follows its final ending.

initial BOM, exact/partial checkpoints, empty strings, dense endings, tabs, Unicode and
lone surrogates. All coordinates, construction pauses and charged index bytes match;
invalid offsets are rejected. A correctness proof alone does not establish a useful
application performance result. The extra following-checkpoint bound is a measured
variant; no unmeasured JIT/deoptimization cause is asserted for its timing difference.

## Preserve semantic work after consumer exceptions — 2026-10-28

An accepted native or packed response clears its running request before notifying
the UI. Previously, an exception from that notification unconditionally failed the
Worker, consuming its restart allowance and potentially terminating newer work started
inside the callback. Both response paths now fail only while they still own the original
running request; after acceptance they resume eligible work through the existing start
guard. Invalid responses still fail normally. Debounce, watchdog, restart limits,
validation, ownership, transport selection and memory allowances are unchanged.

Seven regressions fail against the exact preceding Service body and pass against the
current body: the negative run has 7 failed/32 passed and the positive run has 39 passed.
They cover reentrant request/retry/actual failure, repeated throwing snapshot/error
consumers without exhausting genuine recovery, acknowledged full-to-delta packed
transport, and a real 50,001-block semantic-limit response followed by successful work.
The packed tests check the newest heading, retained caches and complete disposal.

A separate real Electron probe injects one exception immediately after the first
snapshot notification in each source-bound Service variant. The baseline creates two
Workers and sends a redundant full snapshot; the current Service keeps one Worker and
then accepts the next revision as a direct delta. Both variants produce identical full

finishes its existing cleanup chain before rethrowing the original setup exception.

inert. Synchronous channel failure during registration rejects construction instead
of returning a closed adapter. The initial reservation-rejection path remains covered.

## Completed native block handoff — 2026-10-28

The previous goal turn rechecked the already completed root-log migration and made no
application progress. This turn revalidated the native allocation gap and implemented
an internal stream that hands off completed MDAST blocks instead of retaining their
complete root array. The overall delivery goal remains open.

`packages/core/src/markdown-block-stream.ts` provides `markdownBlockSteps`.
It yields complete top-level children in source order and returns complete root metadata,
descriptors, outline, word/character counts, source hash and parser version. It shares
the ordinary parser's frozen conservative grammar selection. Node and descriptor limits
include the same root/traversal semantics, list-item defaults and source limits. Blocks
are described before handoff; prose is accumulated and segmented exactly once at the end.
Consumers must keep candidate results private until the final summary succeeds.

The pinned dependency patch adds a separate lazy generator compiled from the existing
span compiler. Full block tokenization finishes before span resolution, so forward
references and footnotes keep their complete-document meaning. Each span retains the
original handlers, list preparation, shared compiler data and ordinary mutable points.
It checks closed node/token stacks, applies only the audited block-local GFM transform,
detaches completed children and clears each handed-off slot. Unknown transforms or a
replacement root fail. The whitelist comes from a separate GFM-only processor, so a new
application plugin cannot silently become eligible. Cancellation closes nested event
generators and clears remaining children, stacks and temporary compiler data.

The whole-event compiler and existing whole-tree span compiler remain byte-for-byte
recoverable. Both new installed files reconstruct the exact prior span-compiler hashes;
independent reconstruction then checks the original published hashes. Postinstall,
lint/build checks, isolated installation/upgrades, partial installs and CRLF handling
cover the new pinned hashes. `PackedWork` gains a yield type with its existing
`void` default; its revocation and cleanup behavior remains covered by the full suite.

The current inventory binds 493 files: five changed existing inputs and three new files
relative to an augmented 490-file baseline. The inherited 488-file inventory omitted the
patch installer and reconstruction script. Their before-edit archives extend that baseline;

## Complete streamed Markdown packets — 2026-10-28

The internal `packMarkdownDocumentSteps` now encodes completed native parser
children directly into one full SemanticDocument MSP2 packet. The composition preserves
document-wide scalar/schema/position sharing and every document field: complete MDAST,
all position coordinates, extension fields, descriptors, outline, source identity/version,
whole-document counts and actual parser/description timings. Stable private containers
receive final metadata before the encoder visits them. It does not assemble a complete
native children array, and it publishes no packet until parsing and encoding both finish.

Declared `PackedArrayInput` iterators transfer ownership once after registry
validation and admission. Unknown-length inputs require the existing wire, logical working,
node and depth limits. Every pull suspends before its result is encoded. Aliases survive
ordinary identity memo eviction without replaying a consumed iterator. Closure drops source
and completion callbacks, closes unopened inputs, attempts every cleanup and preserves the
original encoding/source failure. The composition accepts revocable PackedWork parser
handles directly, including cancellation before their bodies start.

The experimental producer previously tokenized its complete source before returning control.

The paired pinned patch adds a private document tokenizer generated from the exact installed
`write` and `main` loops. It preserves the original preprocessed chunks, all internal buffer
indexes, lexer state, definitions and serializer. After at most 4,096 root input-code dispatches,

stepping method; ordinary contexts and their synchronous methods retain their behavior and keys.
The private compiler validates its transform whitelist before preprocessing/tokenization and
still waits for complete EOF processing before resolving spans and compiling native blocks.
`markdownBlockSteps` maps the checkpoint to the existing trusted packed-array progress symbol,
which the encoder forwards as an outer yield and never encodes as a JSON element. Timings count
active parser work and exclude suspension. Closure clears pending source chunks and document
events and revokes the complete work/input chain.

## Cooperative whole-value preprocessing — 2026-10-29

The experimental complete block producer now selects a private cooperative preprocessor.
It scans at most 4,096 original UTF-16 source units between scheduling checkpoints while
preserving the exact original literal chunk boundaries, tabs, NUL replacement, BOM, CR/LF
and EOF marker. Tokenization starts after the complete unchanged chunk sequence is ready;
definitions, footnotes, native buffer indexes and all semantic fields retain their behavior.

now pinned and included in independent original-source installation fixtures.

the outer source binding on completion/cancellation. Its scanner can suspend in the middle
of a literal without splitting that literal. Whole-value byte decoding, literal slicing,
chunk-array storage, flow/EOF resolution, span preparation, native blocks/HAST and whole
prose segmentation still have atomic or unadmitted work. A scan-unit bound is not a duration

private cooperative work. Stateless regexes preserve the ordinary guards' exact native
ignore-case semantics. Each slice adds at most 4,089 UTF-16 units and includes up to seven
previous units, keeping every native regex input at or below 4,096 units. The overlap covers
the longest literal prefix (https://). This classification does not split parser input:
the tokenizer/compiler still receives the original complete source and global context.

once all guards are enabled, later source cannot narrow the selection, so classification
can finish early. A separate checkpoint follows completed selection before native parsing.

## Independent cooperative Worker source preparation — 2026-10-29

The experimental Worker's actual message entry now queues an independent source preflight.

metadata before yielding. The source UTF-8 cap and ordinary UTF-16 hash are then checked in
one revocable scan with at most 4,096 reads per advancement. A renderer's claimed digest or
local capability cannot grant completion in the Worker. Only the fully matching result
receives a private WeakSet capability accepted by the prepared producer entry point.

One latest source candidate shares the existing queued callback with the active offer or
cache task. The host alternates those tasks and admits provisional request/source ownership.
Only complete validation and successful promotion admission can revoke the earlier offer.
Bad metadata, bytes, digest, capacity, candidate cancellation or read failure preserve that
offer. Correlated controls cancel the matching candidate or offer; an earlier offer may be
ACKed while a candidate scans. Supersession, failure and disposal close all candidate work.
The host carries numeric progress into the promoted offer without retaining candidate state.

Legacy synchronous prepare/receive APIs preserve their immediate validation behavior. The
new actual Worker path still performs initial request JSON sizing synchronously. The
renderer and Worker each validate their source independently; no wire field or complete
semantic field is removed. Ordinary application transport selection remains unchanged.

## Exact queued request JSON sizing — 2026-10-29

The experimental application path now validates the full request JSON byte cap without
stringifying or encoding its complete source before scheduling. A shared fixed-shape
capture reads known data properties, freezes the request/options and validates bounded
metadata with an empty source. Its exact envelope size includes escaped labels/IDs, JSON
property names, source quotes and numeric spellings. The remaining source budget is checked
independently in both renderer and Worker during the existing 4,096-unit byte/hash scan.
That scan reads each UTF-16 source unit once for UTF-8, JSON spelling and the ordinary digest.

JSON counting handles quote/backslash and short control escapes, six-byte other controls
and lone surrogates, ordinary Unicode and four-byte surrogate pairs. A pending high
surrogate crosses checkpoints without a transient over-count. Only complete validation
can yield an authentic source; cancellation and failure cannot grant partial completion.
The combined scan has no new source-sized JSON string or TextEncoder buffer. It retains
numeric counters instead of adding a separately cached source owner or a second scan.

SemanticService selects postRequestCooperative on the cold and warm packed paths. It sets
up the port before choosing the sizing capability; native and older ports still receive
the complete JSON cap check before any post. The renderer reports an oversized queued
request as a bounded semantic-limit result, releases its provisional ownership and accepts
the next request on the same channel. The Worker independently checks the same envelope
and source; a rejected candidate leaves an earlier valid offer ACKable. Legacy parseRequest,
post, postCooperative, synchronous source construction and producer.prepare preserve their
immediate size/validation behavior, including legacy unknown-property sizing. The internal
fixed-shape request path rejects unknown fields rather than silently excluding their bytes.

## Reuse the last immutable arena field — 2026-10-29

The immutable packed arena now remembers its last successful object-field lookup. This
avoids repeating the shape-key search and decoding preceding references when a guarded
reader asks for the same field again. The cache stores two numeric record IDs and a key
already owned by an admitted shape. Missing/arbitrary query strings, readers, sources,
captures and native document graphs are not stored. Record zero and empty/hostile own
keys remain valid; failed and interleaved queries preserve exact lookup semantics.
Every public read still passes through its existing lifetime guard. Suspended streams
continue to own independent cursors.

The cache adds a fixed 64 logical retained bytes per arena, reserved before index/cache
construction. This deliberately changes arena admission by 64 bytes; it does not establish
physical heap size. All numeric limits remain: 8 MiB wire, 32 MiB encoder working/snapshot,
64 MiB renderer and the existing validator staging/node/depth, slice and watchdog limits.
Encoding admission arguments and suspension points are unchanged. Packed transport remains
experimental and inactive in the ordinary browser endpoint.

## Cooperative native text resolution — 2026-10-29

The experimental complete block producer now opts into _manuslipBlockTextResolveSteps.
The native EOF bridge selects the audited callback by the pinned text-resolver function's
private identity flag, preserves native resolver order and deduplicates function identities.
It yields around other resolver calls; their internal work remains atomic. Ordinary parsing
and private callers without the new option retain the native resolver path. The core callback
adapts micromark 4.0.3's data merging and line-suffix algorithm and includes its MIT notice.

One 256-advance quota covers event walks, trailing whitespace/chunk scans, data merges,
copies and gap edits. Suffix insertions retain the native original indexes and are applied
in reverse order without a whole-event sort. All original points, hard breaks, tabs, final
trailing-whitespace policy and linked-write state remain intact. A revocable work owner drops
input and context on return/throw, including before its first advance; abandoned input is
cleared and partial resolution is never committed. Actual native parent cancellation still
closes the child work and revokes its owned tokenizer context.

read-only configuration and a missing DeepL key. Each state offers a relevant next action.

field after it becomes available. A saved DeepL target has a localized name even before
language discovery. Load cached remains available without a DeepL key or network connection.
Loading settings, opening preferences and changing the reading layout submit no document text.

Settings requests have separate loading/error state and only their latest active owner may
apply a response, rejection or completion. A read failure no longer becomes a missing-provider
error or clears the existing reading copy. Read-only language changes preserve that copy.

and receive a visible notice when saved settings change. Closing preferences removes the key
input so an unsubmitted API key is discarded. Keys remain uncontrolled, write-only DOM values.

processing the next input code. The actual label-end resolveTo identity selects a cooperative
callback; the same input resumes after its resolved array is committed. Ordinary writes,
older callbacks and unknown resolveTo functions retain their native path. Unknown inside-span
resolvers keep the entire native call so they still observe the same global event array.

scanning, image offsets, group/label/text points, array identity, inside-span ordering and
resource/reference events. Label scans/copies/commit, EOF unmatched-marker cleanup and nested

## Recovery loading, retry and keyboard continuity

Recovery now distinguishes draft-list errors from checkpoint-saving errors. If the recovery
directory is unavailable, the panel explains the next step and offers Reload drafts. After
storage is repaired, the same process retries its failed scan through the existing serialized
repository queue. It does not re-offer active checkpoints or claimed drafts. Existing file,
entry, header and body limits and preservation of incompatible files remain unchanged.

A small metadata-only controller admits one recovery action at a time, retains failed entries
for retry and removes a completed entry before refreshing the list. A failed refresh does not
undo a completed restore/discard. Loading no longer delays incoming file opening. Restore and
discard have localized pending/error states, contextual accessible names and a native discard
confirmation that initially focuses Cancel. Cancellation returns focus to the originating row;
successful completion hands it to the next draft or editor. Later user input takes priority
over pending focus restoration. Recovery errors do not expose native exception strings.

concurrent reload/action admission, rejected operations, failed refreshes and explicit retry.

## Canonical sibling key ordering

The experimental resumable encoder now requires sibling names in Object.keys order.
It snapshots and checks names before opening input ownership or starting the encoder.
JavaScript array-index names enumerate first in numeric order; accepting a different
supply order could visit an opaque future sibling before its input existed. Reordered
envelopes and sparse key lists now fail with the explicit invalid-key error. Canonically
ordered numeric names, non-index numeric spellings, empty names and own __proto__/
constructor/toString fields retain exact checkpoints and canonical final packets.

against the archived prior implementation; the current focused suite passes 2,830
checks. Complete producer verification passes 6,756 exact canonical packet comparisons

## Projection reservation reuse and fixed local limits — 2026-10-30

`ProjectionWorkspace` now captures its numeric retained/staging limits at construction.
Later mutation of a caller's limits object cannot enlarge that local allowance. Once
the capture is checked and a request passes the original numeric/local-budget checks,
a private reservation can cover another request in the same 64 KiB quantum. This
avoids repeating a ledger resize whose byte charges would be identical. Growth and
shrink still resize normally, and a rejected growth never advances the logical plan.

Admission callbacks keep their original workspace `this` binding, run on every
request and retain the complete resize path. Such a callback can refuse admission or
reentrantly close a workspace, capture or owner. Those operations must still reject;
the reuse path applies only when no callback can revoke the private reservation
between the capture guard and reuse. No reservation handle escapes this class.

Ten new unit cases cover binding, fixed limits after caller mutation, occupied
aggregate staging and rollback/retry, original callback failures, and revocation
through all three owners with and without an admission callback. All 172 focused
cases pass. The complete suite passes 19,514 cases in 214 files, with the single
preexisting Windows skip for restrictive POSIX permission bits. Static checks pass.

A frozen-source complete receiver probe validates all six unchanged 1 MiB corpora
against independently generated native snapshots. Source/semantic hashes, every
projection reservation decision, all non-projection resize arguments and original
outer yields agree. Ledgers return to their initial values after validation and to
zero on disposal. The number of avoided resizes is exactly the number of requests
already covered by the private reservation:

| Single paragraph | 17 | 11 | 6 | 22,743 |
| Mixed RTL | 12,522 | 5,693 | 6,829 | 35,390 |
| Repeated paragraphs | 178,209 | 81,623 | 96,586 | 401,480 |
| Many small blocks | 211,642 | 96,954 | 114,688 | 476,737 |

## Pending native input across document transitions — 2026-10-30

Creating or activating a document could destroy its current CodeMirror view before
pending native DOM input reached the editor state. A document that appeared clean
could also be locked for close before that input made it dirty. An adversarial
packaged regression now holds native mutation delivery and animation frames, inserts
` pending 世界`, then requests a transition. The previous directory application
reproducibly returns to `# Original\n\nKeep this text.` with that suffix missing.
The baseline test, failed report and trace are retained.

`DocumentController.synchronizeInput()` exposes the existing public CodeMirror
measurement boundary used by Save. Document activation, document creation/opening
and close decisions await it before replacing the view or changing editability.
Rapid activation requests keep the last requested tab. A queued file command waits
for a preceding activation, so immediately saving a requested tab saves that tab's
body. Closing still uses the existing cancellation, locking and file-operation
queue. No private editor observer API or contenteditable serialization enters the
application.

Five additional unit cases cover latest-request selection, immediate Save ordering,
input arriving while an open dialog loads, and both tab/window close decisions.
All 27 focused cases pass. The full suite passes 19,519 cases across 214 files;
its single preexisting Windows skip checks restrictive POSIX permission bits.
Static checks pass. The final pending-input integration set passes all five cases:
Save, New with retained undo/redo and exact saved text, mouse tab activation, and
cancelling both document and window close after the delayed input makes them dirty.

The first candidate integration set passed three cases and failed two. Its redo
assertion used Ctrl+Shift+Z on Windows instead of the app's Ctrl+Y binding. The mouse
case's fixture had not finished initial editor focus: a traced CodeMirror focus
update cleared its artificially held mutation before pointerdown even arrived.
Waiting for the observable focused editor class before inserting held input makes
that scenario pass against the same application bytes. The fixture keeps its held
mutation/frame controls, pre-transition assertions, exact saved-source comparison
and original deadline. This does not justify a tab pointer/focus workaround.
The corrected fixture still reproduces real transition loss in the previous build.

results neither identify the earlier extra characters nor close general input/IME
reliability acceptance.

## 2026-10-31 — Exact restricted ASCII counting during semantic validation

The complete prose validator still constructs one runtime-default whole-string
Intl.Segmenter result, keeps its existing storage admission and checks the exact
supplied word count. It now recognizes a deliberately restricted complete ASCII
language: contiguous letter/digit runs separated by whitespace or ASCII hyphens,
with only ! , . : ; ? around a run. A second alphanumeric run across punctuation,
unsupported ASCII, Unicode or a surrogate uses the original complete native
iterator. The scanner yields every 4,096 UTF-16 units, uses constant scratch and
does not truncate, normalize or sum per-block counts. Native fallback retains its
sixteen-next-per-advance limit. Existing caps, grammar, clocks and experimental
activation flags are unchanged. Word-boundary reasoning uses
[UAX29 WB5/8/9/10 and the default-breaking hyphen rule](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/#Word_Boundary_Rules);
this restricted recognizer is not a replacement Unicode segmenter.

The initial attempt skipped construction of the native result and failed three
existing focused contract tests; its new test also had two non-null assertion lint

A future protocol should synchronously capture renderer numeric counters at the hook and retain the later observation separately. It should also count actual field-cache misses: the shared reference mode clears the field shape, so header savings can replace a useful field cursor. Call totals alone do not measure that tradeoff.

their counts match; the staged large-paste path repeated the entire clipboard at each range.

the events are explicitly untrusted. This does not validate physical input or OS clipboard
ownership, or explain the historical Pipeline66 extra-character failure.

range, per-insertion cursor lengths and native by-line cursor association. It keeps the main
selection, mapped original ranges, private cooperative preparation, cancellation, document
byte cap and single isolated input.paste transaction. Mismatched plain counts and multiline
rich-text conversion retain whole-input replication. No whole-clipboard join/split, semantic,

## Iteration101 — optional local Pandoc and editable document export

ADR002 item25 is accepted on the Windows baseline. Source and reading actions offer
DOCX, EPUB and a LaTeX-source/media ZIP, with Standard and Numbered headings + contents
profiles. A native picker explicitly selects a trusted Pandoc3 executable. Main owns
its canonical path, streaming fingerprint, version probe and atomic versioned profile;
the renderer receives only its name/version. Change, Forget, failed-save Retry and
session-only/future-schema states remain usable. Tool replacement requires re-selection.
No Pandoc binary, new dependency, arbitrary argument, filter, shell or PDF engine is bundled.
The external executable retains the user's OS privileges; Pandoc's sandbox is not an OS sandbox.

Conversion uses the existing immutable, sanitized source/reading capture and bounded
asset/print preparation. Text, tables and notes remain editable. Native captures preserve
math, chemistry and diagram glyphs as PNGs. Side-by-side rows become two-column tables;
interlinear pairs retain visible labels. All formats use their own document styles.
LaTeX includes referenced media and compilation instructions, not a compiled PDF.
Stale-reading confirmation retains the clicked copy and starts no translation request.
Argument arrays, restricted environment, owned temporary files, stream/heap limits and
deadlines bound the child. Cancel/close/error remains charged until child closure.
The existing terminable export worker validates complete containers, sizes, CRCs and
every expected image before fingerprint-checked atomic publication. Existing files and
source remain intact on failures. Existing source/asset caps and all20 parser pins remain.

Repository checks, production build and directory packaging pass. The full unit run
passes19,866/19,867 assertions across237 files, with one existing Windows skip; all12

source CRLF preservation, unchanged editor DOM, multiple selections and undo/save.

test/artifacts/logs/pipeline101-ui-review.md. The corresponding locale media hashes match exactly.
