## Iteration102 — versioned local command plugins

ADR002 item26 is accepted on the Windows baseline. Preferences installs a bounded local
JSON bundle after explicit permission review, with every grant initially unchecked.
Installed manifest/code bytes and their fingerprint bind grants to the reviewed version.
Explicit updates require fresh grants. Enable/disable, permission changes and confirmed
removal persist atomically; errors retain the old installation. Corrupt/future registry
recovery remains visible. API1 and a complete working bundle are documented in PLUGINS.md.

Each explicit command runs in a fresh sandboxed Chromium renderer, private session and
origin with a verified process distinct from the editor. Its frozen preload exposes
only registration and bounded text file/network operations. No Node or editor bridge is
available. Direct networking, navigation, windows, workers and resource loading are denied.
File access requires a grant and a native choice for each action; writes reject any open
document destination. The main-owned network proxy accepts only approved exact origins,
GET/POST and bounded text, without redirects or application credentials. Revoked responses
are cancelled even if fetch settles during cancellation. A 15-second deadline includes
initial loading/registration; jobs stay charged through host and native-picker settlement.
Disable, grant changes, update, removal and owner closure revoke active capabilities.
New commands cannot start while installation mutations are still pending.

Commands capture source text/selections only with read access. Inspection returns plain
text; transforms return inert proposals. Apply checks the current enabled installation,
fingerprint, write grant and captured document revision after pending input settles, then
commits one undoable source change. Changed source and revoked grants prevent application.
The editor can save while a plugin process is hung; process termination leaves it usable.

Repository checks and the production build pass. The final full unit run passes
19,883/19,884 assertions across242 files, with one existing Windows skip. Actual optional
Pandoc conversions remain enabled. The final package passes171/171 desktop cases with
zero retries/skips. Seven plugin flows cover install/restart/update/disable/remove,
denied and granted native file/network actions, redirects/unlisted origins, real hung
and loading-timeout processes, cancellation during a native save picker, stale proposals,
CRLF save and exact undo. Seventeen new unit assertions include storage/fingerprint
recovery, caps/stream cleanup, cancellation during input and permission mutation races.

Twelve final wide/400px screenshots cover installation review, installed state and
proposed edits in English/light and Chinese/dark. All have zero axe violations and root
overflow, with retained accessibility trees and direct visual review. Selecting a bundle
focuses and reveals its permission review. The taller Preferences dialog now explicitly
wraps focus between enabled visible controls. Native keyboard tests retain the toolbar
order including Plugin commands. Review is intest/artifacts/logs/pipeline102-ui-review.md and bound
captures/probes intest/artifacts/logs/pipeline102-interface-artifacts.json.

Earlier evidence remains retained: the first full package passed168 cases and exposed
Preferences' extra scroll-container Tab stop plus the old toolbar-order expectation.
The final package fixes the former and explicitly tests the new button in sequence.
Review also found and fixed execution during pending grant persistence and a permission
check preceding input settlement. Fixture word-count/newline expectations and Electron
picker types were corrected. No source cap, parser pin, retry policy or assertion was removed.

## Iteration103 — explicit folder and WebDAV file sync

ADR002 item27 is accepted on the Windows baseline. Document actions → Sync pairs a
saved document with one file in a native-selected folder or one exact WebDAV URL.
Connections retain atomic persistent baselines and interrupted-transfer intent;
review, send, receive, keep-local/export-remote/send, retry and disconnect are explicit.
Opening the app/dialog makes no network request. HTTPS, conditional PUT, exact URL
scope, bounded streams and credential isolation apply. SYNC.md and ADR012 document
the supported contract and limits.

Every replacement first preserves the overwritten raw bytes in durable, verified
recovery storage. Copies remain after disconnect and can be exported or explicitly
removed. Damaged/pending artifacts stay visible and block new replacement. Stale
review, cancellation, failed persistence and changed remote/local bytes prevent unsafe
publication. Inbound writes share normal file-session queues: clean editors reload,
while newer dirty drafts and active compositions retain their text with explicit
external-change conflict controls. Credentials stay in main memory unless secure
key-store persistence is explicitly selected; plaintext never enters saved JSON or replies.

Repository checks and the production build pass. One final full unit run passes
19,921/19,922 assertions across 251 files, with one existing Windows POSIX skip and
all 12 actual optional Pandoc conversions enabled. The final package passes 177/177
desktop cases with zero retries/skips: all 171 previous cases and six new sync flows.
These cover both adapters, exact BOM/CRLF bytes, offline retry, restart, conditional
write races, keep-both native export, recovery export/removal, disconnect, keyboard
focus and dirty/composition download races. New units cover strict IPC, folder identity,
atomic registry recovery, raw recovery/caps, credential revocation/deadlines, native
picker cancellation and interrupted intent. No previous assertion or source cap was removed.

All 16 final wide/400px screenshots in English/light and Chinese/dark were directly

test/artifacts/logs/pipeline103-packaged-interface-artifacts.json.

## Iteration104 — Windows deliverable and separate release hooks

ADR002 item28 is accepted on the Windows baseline. Items20–28 are implemented and
verified under the documented feature-delivery priority. The functional editor,
workspace, source/Live/translated modes, bilingual layouts/export, advanced editing,
plugins and explicit sync are included in the retained unsigned local installer.
The historical broader qualification gates retain their scope; they are not silently
marked as platform, physical AT/IME or perfect-performance acceptance.

Ordinary builds explicitly disable publisher inference and pass --publish never.
A separate package:release command supports review without execution (--plan),
credential-required Windows/macOS signing (--signed), optional explicit HTTPS feed
metadata (--updates), fresh output, artifact checksums and failure reports. It accepts
no publish/cross-host arguments. Code-signing/notarization credentials remain in the
environment; configuration and reports contain no secret values. The actual local
update-metadata run emitted latest.yml, a blockmap and app-update.yml; its SHA-512
matches the generated installer, and its application ASAR exactly matches the ordinary
deliverable. It uploaded nothing. The ordinary installer has no configured update feed;
there is no installed automatic-update runtime. DISTRIBUTION.md and ADR013 describe
the hooks, supported targets and current manual installer-update path.

The existing four-target CI remains: Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS x64 and macOS arm64.
It builds once and reuses archived artifacts for desktop tests. Release-profile schema
and credential/feed/CLI tests now run in CI; all four pass locally with the installed
electron-builder26 schema. Five Linux launcher tests remain Linux-only and skip on this
Windows host. Other-platform CI execution is not claimed here.

The final NSIS installer was executed in a fresh ignored directory. All 78 installed
runtime files exactly match the verified unpacked build; the only extra file is the
uninstaller. Two actual installed-app launches verify packaged ASAR startup and exact
UTF-8 BOM/CRLF/Unicode edit/save/reopen. Installer, application and uninstaller contain
the expected seven icon sizes. Per-user registration, Open With advertisement and
shortcuts are checked without changing the default Markdown application. Uninstall
removes its fresh installation and restores the complete prior registration/shortcut/
association state. Evidence: test/packaging/results/windows-installer-38b6103e-b32b-42e0-a5e7-e9f2551b8b0c/report.json.

The final full unit run passes 19,924/19,925 assertions across 251 files, with the one
existing Windows POSIX permission skip. All actual optional Pandoc conversions remain
enabled. The final package passes all 177 desktop cases with zero retries/skips and
all previous cases retained. Repository checks and the production build pass. Three
new unit cases cover strict-preload input errors, cancellation of a rejected request
and exact recovery bytes for a long Unicode filename whose display label crosses a
surrogate boundary. Sync invalid destinations now show an input error; recovery labels
stay well-formed without changing the original filename or document bytes.

The earlier full run passed 176 cases and exposed a tab focus race at narrow width.

the handler now accepts only plain Tab/Shift+Tab, preserving native document cycling.
All failure traces remain retained. The complete correction
passes the original assertions plus rapid Home/End/Tab/Shift+Tab loops, both themes,
Chinese, 320px width and native 200% zoom. No timeout, retry, source cap or assertion
was removed to pass the final suite.
